questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation $( y - 2{\log}_{e}x ) dx + ( x{\log}_{e}{x}^{2} ) dy = 0, x > 1$ passes through the points $\left(e, \dfrac{4}{3}\right) and ( {e}^{4}, \alpha )$, then $\alpha$ is equal to $_______$
questions.solution:
Given,

$( y - 2{\log}_{e}x ) dx + ( x{\log}_{e}{x}^{2} ) dy = 0, x > 1$

$⇒ 2xlnx\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 2lnx\left\{\text{where}{\log}_{e}x = lnx\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{2xlnx} = \dfrac{1}{x}$

Which is linear differential equation,

So, $I . F = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{2xlnx}} = \sqrt{lnx}$

Now, solution of the equation is given by,

$y \cdot \sqrt{lnx} = ∫ \dfrac{\sqrt{lnx}}{x}dx$

$⇒ y \cdot \sqrt{lnx} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(lnx\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + C . . . ( i )$

Given, $eq . ( i )$ passes through point $\left(e, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$

So, $C = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Hence, solution of differential equation will be,

$y\sqrt{lnx} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(lnx\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

Also given, above equation passes through point $( {e}^{4}, \alpha )$

$\alpha\sqrt{ln{e}^{4}} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(ln{e}^{4}\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ 2\alpha = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(4\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 8 + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 3$

questions.solution:
The given differential equation is

$\left(1 + ln\left(x\right)\right)\dfrac{dx}{dy} - xln\left(x\right) = {e}^{y}$

Put $xln\left(x\right) = t$

$⇒ \left(1 + ln\left(x\right)\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} - t = {e}^{y}$ which is a linear differential equation.

$I . F = {e}^{- ∫ dy}$

$= {e}^{- y}$

The solution of the differential equation is

$⇒ t \times {e}^{- y} = ∫ {e}^{y} \times {e}^{- y}dy + c$

$⇒ t \times {e}^{- y} = y + c$

$⇒ xln\left(x\right) = y{e}^{y} + c{e}^{y}$

Put $x = 1, y = 0$

$⇒ c = 0$

Put $x = a, y = 2$

$aln\left(a\right) = 2{e}^{2}$

$∴ {a}^{a} = {e}^{2{e}^{2}}$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be a solution of the differential equation $( xcosx ) dy + ( xysinx + ycosx - 1 ) dx = 0, 0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$ If $\dfrac{\pi}{3}y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3},$ then $\left|\dfrac{\pi}{6}{y}^{"}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + 2{y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right|$ is equal to $_______ .$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left(xcosx\right)dy + \left(xysinx + ycosx - 1\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ \left(xcosx\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(yxsinx + ycosx\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(\dfrac{xsinx + cosx}{xcosx}\right) = \dfrac{1}{xcosx}$

Which is a linear differential equation of form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P\left(x\right)y = Q\left(x\right)$

Now we know that integrating factor will be ${e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ \left(tanx + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx} = {e}^{ln\left|secx\right| + lnx} = x \cdot secx$

Hence, solution of linear differential equation is given by,

$⇒ y \cdot xsecx = ∫ \dfrac{xsecx}{xcosx}dx$

$⇒ xysecx = tanx + C$

Now using $\dfrac{\pi}{3}y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{3}y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)sec\dfrac{\pi}{3} = tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} + C$

$⇒ C = \sqrt{3}$

Hence, $xysecx = tanx + \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ xy\left(x\right) = 2sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ x{y}^{'}\left(x\right) + y\left(x\right) = 2cos\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

Now again differentiating we get,

$⇒ x{y}^{"} ( x ) + 2{y}^{'} ( x ) = - 2sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

Thus $\dfrac{\pi}{6}{y}^{"}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + 2{y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = - 2$

Hence $\left|\dfrac{\pi}{6}{y}^{"}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + 2{y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right| = 2$

questions.q: Let $\alphax = exp\left({x}^{\beta}{y}^{\gamma}\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2{x}^{2}ydy - \left(1 - x{y}^{2}\right)dx = 0$, $x > 0, y\left(2\right) = \sqrt{{\log}_{e}2}$. Then $\alpha + \beta - \gamma$ equals :
questions.solution:
Given the solution of differential equation,

$\alphax = {e}^{{x}^{\beta} \cdot {y}^{\gamma}} . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Now calculating the solution of differential equation,

$2{x}^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - x{y}^{2}$

Let ${y}^{2} = t ⇒ 2\dfrac{d y}{d x} = \dfrac{d t}{d x}$

$∴ {x}^{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 1 - xt$

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} . . . . . ( 2 )$

Above differential equation is linear in $t$

We know solutions of differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$ is given by,

$y . {e}^{∫ Pdx} = ∫ Q . {e}^{∫ Pdx} + C ( {e}^{∫ Pdx} = I . F . )$

Now calculating, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = {e}^{lnx} = x$

Therefore, the solution of equation $\left(2\right)$ is given by,

$t . x = ∫ \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} \cdot xdx + C$

$⇒ {y}^{2} \cdot x = lnx + C$

$∵ y ( 2 ) = \sqrt{ln2}$

$∴ 2 . ln2 = ln2 + C ⇒ C = ln2$

Hence, solution is $x{y}^{2} = lnx + ln2$

$⇒ x{y}^{2} = ln2x$

$⇒ 2x = {e}^{x \cdot {y}^{2}} . . . . . . ( 3 )$

On comparing equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(3\right)$ we get,

$\alpha = 2, \beta = 1, \gamma = 2$

$∴ \alpha + \beta - \gamma = 1$

Then solution of differential equation is

$y\left(secx\right) = ∫ x{sec}^{2}xdx$

$⇒ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ∫ tanxdx$

$⇒ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ln\left(secx\right) + C$

Given:

$y\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

$∴ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ln\left(secx\right) + 1$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, we get

$y\left(sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - ln\left(sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) + 1$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) - ln\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + 1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{12} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}ln\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{12} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left[ln\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) - lne\right]$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{12} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2}{e\sqrt{3}}\right)$

questions.q: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(t\right)dt$. If $f\left(0\right) = {e}^{- 2}$, then $2f\left(0\right) - f\left(2\right)$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Let

${∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(t\right)dt = k$

$y = f\left(x\right)$

Now, we have

$f\left(x\right) + {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(t\right)dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = k$

This is a linear differential equation.

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ dx} = {e}^{x}$

Solution of the given differential equation is

$y{e}^{x} = k ∫ {e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{x} = k{e}^{x} + C$

Now, $f\left(0\right) = {e}^{- 2}$, so

$C = {e}^{- 2} - k$

Hence,

$y{e}^{x} = k{e}^{x} + \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right)$

$⇒ y = f\left(x\right) = k + \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right){e}^{- x} . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now,

$k = {∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(t\right)dt$

$⇒ k = {∫}_{0}^{2}\left[k + \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right){e}^{- t}\right]dt$

$⇒ k = {\left[kt - \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right){e}^{- t}\right]}_{0}^{2}$

$⇒ k = 2k - \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right)\left({e}^{- 2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left({e}^{- 2} - k\right)\left({e}^{- 2} - 1\right) = k$

$⇒ k = \left({e}^{- 2} - 1\right)$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = \left({e}^{- 2} - 1\right) + {e}^{- x}$

$∴ f\left(2\right) = 2{e}^{- 2} - 1$

$f\left(0\right) = {e}^{- 2}$

So,

$2f\left(0\right) - f\left(2\right) = 1$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ such that $y ( 1 ) = 1$. Then $\left|( y ( 2 ) {)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right|$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y\left(5{x}^{2} - 3{y}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)}$

This is homogeneous differential equation

Let $y = tx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{( tx ) \left(5{x}^{2} - 3{t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{t\left(5 - 3{t}^{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{5t - 3{t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}} - t = \dfrac{3t - {t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

Taking integration on both sides we get,

$∫ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let $3t - {t}^{3} = z ⇒ 3\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = dz$

$⇒ \left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = \dfrac{1}{3}dz$

Substitute in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{2}{3} ∫ \dfrac{dz}{z} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}ln ( z ) = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ z\dfrac{2}{3} = cx ⇒ z = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3t - {t}^{3} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Now put $t = \dfrac{y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Given $y ( 1 ) = 1$ when $x = 1, y = 1$

$⇒ c\dfrac{3}{2} = 2$

So, equation becomes $3\dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = 2x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2}y - {y}^{3} = 2x\dfrac{9}{2} . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Put $x = 2$ in equation $\left(2\right)$,

$12y ( 2 ) - {\left(y ( 2 )\right)}^{3} = 2 ( 2) \dfrac{9}{2} = 32\sqrt{2}$

questions.question: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ such that $y ( 1 ) = 1$. Then $\left|( y ( 2 ) {)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right|$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y\left(5{x}^{2} - 3{y}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)}$

This is homogeneous differential equation

Let $y = tx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{( tx ) \left(5{x}^{2} - 3{t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{t\left(5 - 3{t}^{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{5t - 3{t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}} - t = \dfrac{3t - {t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

Taking integration on both sides we get,

$∫ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let $3t - {t}^{3} = z ⇒ 3\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = dz$

$⇒ \left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = \dfrac{1}{3}dz$

Substitute in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{2}{3} ∫ \dfrac{dz}{z} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}ln ( z ) = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ z\dfrac{2}{3} = cx ⇒ z = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3t - {t}^{3} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Now put $t = \dfrac{y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Given $y ( 1 ) = 1$ when $x = 1, y = 1$

$⇒ c\dfrac{3}{2} = 2$

So, equation becomes $3\dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = 2x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2}y - {y}^{3} = 2x\dfrac{9}{2} . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Put $x = 2$ in equation $\left(2\right)$,

$12y ( 2 ) - {\left(y ( 2 )\right)}^{3} = 2 ( 2) \dfrac{9}{2} = 32\sqrt{2}$

$∴ \left|{\left(y ( 2 )\right)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right| = 32\sqrt{2}$

questions.solution:
Given,

Differential equation,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} + 3{y}^{2}}{3{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right) \text{ and } y\left(1\right) = 0$

Now let $y = vx$

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - \left(\dfrac{1 + 3{v}^{2}}{3 + {v}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - \dfrac{{\left(v + 1\right)}^{3}}{3 + {v}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(3 + {v}^{2}\right)dv}{{\left(v + 1\right)}^{3}} + \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{4dv}{{\left(v + 1\right)}^{3}} + ∫ \dfrac{dv}{v + 1} - ∫ \dfrac{2dv}{{\left(v + 1\right)}^{2}} + ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2}{{\left(v + 1\right)}^{2}} + ln\left|v + 1\right| + \dfrac{2}{v + 1} + ln\left|x\right| = c$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2{x}^{2}}{{\left(x + y\right)}^{2}} + ln\left|\dfrac{x + y}{x}\right| + \dfrac{2x}{x + y} + ln\left|x\right| = c$

$⇒ \dfrac{2xy}{{\left(x + y\right)}^{2}} + ln\left|x + y\right| = c$

$∵ y\left(1\right) = 0$

$∴ c = 0$, as $x = 1, y = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{2xy}{{\left(x + y\right)}^{2}} + ln\left|x + y\right| = 0$

Then $y ( 1 )$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{- 3{x}^{5}\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3}\right)}{{\left(1 + {x}^{6}\right)}^{3 / 2}}\right)y = 2x{e}^{\left\{\dfrac{{x}^{3} - \tan^{- 1}{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{6}}}\right\}}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$.

Hence,

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{- 3{x}^{5}\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3}}{{\left(1 + {x}^{6}\right)}^{3 / 2}}dx}$

Put $\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} = u ⇒ \left(\dfrac{3{x}^{2}}{1 + {x}^{6}}\right)dx = du$

$I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{utanu}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^{2}u}}du}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{utanu}{secu}du}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ usinudu}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{- \left[- ucosu + ∫ cosudu\right]}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{ucosu - sinu}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{\left\{\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right) - \left(\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right)\right\}}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right\}}$

Solution of differential equation is

$y \cdot e\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}} = ∫ 2x{e}^{\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} - \tan^{- 1}{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right)} \cdot {e}^{\left(\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}\left({x}^{3}\right) - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right)}dx$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right\}} = ∫ 2xdx$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right\}} = {x}^{2} + C$

Also, it passes through the origin then $C = 0$, hence

$y{e}^{\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}{x}^{3} - {x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{6}}}\right\}} = {x}^{2}$

Now, put $x = 1$, then we get

$y\left(1\right)e\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}\left(1\right) - 1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1\right)e\dfrac{\pi - 4}{4\sqrt{2}} = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{{e}^{\left(\dfrac{\pi - 4}{4\sqrt{2}}\right)}}$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = e\dfrac{4 - \pi}{4\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$  be the solution of the differential equation $x{\log}_{e}x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = {x}^{2}{\log}_{e}x, ( x > 1 )$. If $y ( 2 ) = 2$, then $y ( e )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$xlnx\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = {x}^{2}lnx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{xlnx} = x$

This is a linear differential equation.

Now, finding integrating factor we get

$I . F = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{xlnx}dx} = {e}^{ln\left(lnx\right)} = lnx$

Now, solution of the differential equation is given by

$y \times I . F = ∫ \left(x \times I . F\right)dx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = ∫ xlnxdx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + c$

Now given $y\left(2\right) = 2$,

$2 \times ln2 = ln2 \cdot \dfrac{{2}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{2}^{2}}{4} + c$

$⇒ c = 1$

So, equation will be $y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + 1$

Now finding $y\left(e\right)$ we get,

$y \times lne = lne \cdot \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{4} + 1$

$⇒ y \times 1 = 1 \cdot \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{4} + 1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4 + {e}^{2}}{4}$

questions.solution:

So, the equation of curve becomes~${log}_{e}x - \dfrac{1}{x} = {log}_{e}y - 2$

$⇒ y = e^{lnx} - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2$

Hence,~$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}e^{lnx - 1} - \dfrac{1}{x} + 2= e^{- \infty}= 0$.

questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} + \alphay = \gamma \cdot {e}^{- \betat}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So, integrating factor will be $I . F = {e}^{∫ \alphadt} = {e}^{\alphat}$

So, the solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ {e}^{- \betat} \times {e}^{\alphat}$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ {e}^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\alphat} = \gamma\dfrac{{e}^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c$

$⇒ y = \gamma\dfrac{{e}^{- \betat}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c{e}^{- \alphat}$

Now finding $\lim_{t \to \infty}y$ we get,

$\lim_{t \to \infty}y = \lim_{t \to \infty}\left(\gamma\dfrac{{e}^{- \betat}}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)} + c{e}^{- \alphat}\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{t \to \infty}y = \gamma \times 0 + c \times 0 = 0\left\{\text{as}{e}^{- \infty} \to 0\right\}$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$  be the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\left(1 + {x}^{2}\left(1 + {\log}_{e}x\right)\right)$, $x > 0, y ( 1 ) = 3$. Then $\dfrac{{y}^{2} ( x )}{9}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given differential equation can be rewritten as,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x} = {y}^{3}\left(1 + {\log}_{e}x\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{{y}^{3}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{{xy}^{2}} = 1 + {\log}_{e}x$

Let $\left(- \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}\right) = t ⇒ \dfrac{2}{{y}^{3}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$∴ \dfrac{dt}{2dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \left(1 + {\log}_{e}x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{2t}{x} = 2\left(1 + {\log}_{e}x\right) . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

We know the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$ is given by,

${ye}^{∫ Pdx} = ∫ {Qe}^{∫ Pdx} + C ( WhereI . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx} )$

Therefore, on solving equation(1) we get,

I.F.$= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = {x}^{2}$

$\dfrac{- {x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\left(1 + {\log}_{e}x\right){x}^{3} - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right) + C . . . . . . ( 2 )$

Given,$y ( 1 ) = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{9} = - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) + C$

$∴ C = \dfrac{5}{9}$

Now putting value of C in equation(2) we get,

$\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{5 - 2{x}^{3}\left(2 + {\log}_{e}{x}^{3}\right)}$

questions.solution:
Given differential equation is

${x}^{3}dy + \left(xy - 1\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}$

This is a linear differential equation.

If $IF = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}dx} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}$

Solution of a given linear differential equation is

$y{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = ∫ {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}\left(\dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)dx$

Put $- \dfrac{1}{x} = t ⇒ \dfrac{dx}{{x}^{2}} = dt$

$⇒ y{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = - ∫ {e}^{- t}tdt$

$⇒ y{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = t{e}^{- t} + {e}^{- t} + C$

$⇒ y = t + 1 + Ce\dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{x} + 1 + Ce\dfrac{1}{x}$

Put $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, then

$3 - e = 2 + 1 + C{e}^{2}$

$C = - \dfrac{1}{e}$

So,

$y = \dfrac{1}{x} + 1 - \dfrac{1}{e}\left(e\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$

So,

$y\left(1\right) = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1$

questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y}$ passes through the point $\left(2, 1\right) and \left(k + 1, 2\right), k > 0$, then
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y - 2}{x - y} = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) - \left(y - 1\right)}$

Now let $x - 1 = X, y - 1 = Y$

So, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{X + Y}{X - Y} . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let $Y = VX\dfrac{dY}{dX} = V + X\dfrac{dV}{dX}$

Putting the value in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$V + X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{1 + V}{1 - V}$

$⇒ X\dfrac{dV}{dX} = \dfrac{{V}^{2} + 1}{1 - V}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{1 - V}{1 + {V}^{2}}dV = ∫ \dfrac{dX}{X}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dV}{1 + {V}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{2VdV}{1 + {V}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{dX}{X}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}V - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + {V}^{2}\right) = lnX + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + \dfrac{{Y}^{2}}{{X}^{2}}\right) = ln\left(X\right) + c$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y - 1}{x - 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1 + \dfrac{{\left(y - 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}}\right) = ln\left(x - 1\right) + c$

Now given curve passes through $\left(2, 1\right)$

So, $0 - \dfrac{1}{2}ln1 = ln1 + c ⇒ c = 0$

Now given curve also passes through $\left(k + 1, 2\right)$

So, $\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}$ In $\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{k}^{2}}\right) = lnk$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) =$ In $\left(\dfrac{1 + {k}^{2}}{{k}^{2}}\right) + 2lnk$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right) =$ In $\left(1 + {k}^{2}\right)$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}\right)y = \dfrac{\left(x + 3\right)}{x + 1}, x > - 1$, which passes through the point $\left(0, 1\right)$. Then $y\left(1\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}\right)y = \dfrac{x + 3}{x + 1}$

Now comparing with $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \times p\left(x\right) = q\left(x\right)$
We get $p\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}$

So $IF = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{{x}^{3} + 6{x}^{2} + 11x + 6}dx}$

Now finding the integration we get,

$∫ p\left(x\right)dx = ∫ \dfrac{\left(2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13\right)dx}{\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 2\right)\left(x + 3\right)}$

Using partial fraction we get,

$\dfrac{2{x}^{2} + 11x + 13}{\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 2\right)\left(x + 3\right)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 2} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3}$

On solving we get A = $\dfrac{4}{2} =$2$, $B = 1 and C = - 1$

So, $∫ p$\left(x\right)$dx = Aln$\left(x + 1\right)$ + Bln$\left(x + 2\right)$ + cln$\left(x + 3\right)$

$= ln \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)$}^{2}$\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right)$

So, $IF = {e}^{∫ p\left(x\right)dx} = \dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 3\right)}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times IF = ∫ Q \times IFdx$

$⇒ y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 3}{x + 1}\right)\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x + 3\right)}dx$

$⇒ y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3{x}^{2}}{2} + 2x + c$

Now given curve passes through $\left(0, 1\right)$,

So, $⇒ 1 \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(0 + 1\right)}^{2}\left(0 + 2\right)}{0 + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{0}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3 \times {0}^{2}}{2} + 2 \times 0 + c ⇒ c = \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, curve becomes $y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}\left(x + 2\right)}{x + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3{x}^{2}}{2} + 2x + \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now put $x = 1$ we get, $y \times \left(\dfrac{{\left(1 + 1\right)}^{2}\left(1 + 2\right)}{1 + 3}\right) = \dfrac{{1}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{3 \times {1}^{2}}{2} + 2 \times 1 + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ y \times 3 = 1 + \dfrac{3}{2} + 2 ⇒ y \times 3 = \dfrac{9}{2}$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.solution:

So integrating factor is ${e}^{∫ 1 \cdot dx} = {e}^{x}$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}$\left(y \cdot {e}^{x}\right)$ = \lim_{x \to \infty}$\left(\tan^{- 1}\left({e}^{x}\right)$ + $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$\right) = $\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}

$

Now putting $x = 8$, we get

$\dfrac{\sqrt{7}y\left(8\right)}{3} = 8 - 4ln3 + 2ln3 - \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ \sqrt{7}y\left(8\right) = 19 - 6ln3$

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the points $\left(0, 2\right)$ and $\left(0, - 2\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given a circle passing through $\left(0, - 2\right)$ and $\left(0, 2\right)$, so its equation will be,

$\left(x - {x}_{1}\right)\left(x - {x}_{2}\right) + \left(y - {y}_{1}\right)\left(y - {y}_{2}\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left|\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ {x}_{1} & {y}_{1} & 1 \\ {x}_{2} & {y}_{2} & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0, \left({\lambda}_{1} \in R\right)$

On putting the given values we get,

$⇒ \left(x - 0\right)\left(x - 0\right) + \left(y - 2\right)\left(y + 2\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left|\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0, \left({\lambda}_{1} \in R\right)$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \left({y}^{2} - 4\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left(4x\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \left({y}^{2} - 4\right) + \lambdax = 0, \left(\lambda \in R\right)$

Now dividing both side by $x$ we get,

questions.q: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $xdy = \left(\sqrt{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}} + y\right)dx, x > 0$, intersect the line $x = 1$ at $y = 0$ and the line $x = 2$ at $y = \alpha$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$xdy = \left(\sqrt{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}} + y\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy - ydx = \sqrt{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{\sqrt{1 + {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{\sqrt{1 + {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left(\dfrac{y}{x} + \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2} + 1}\right) = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{y + \sqrt{{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}}}{x} = cx$

$⇒ y + \sqrt{{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}} = c{x}^{2}$

Now given when $x = 1, y = 0 ⇒ 0 + 1 = c ⇒ c = 1$

So equation of curve is $y + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}} = {x}^{2}$

Now at $x = 2, y = \alpha$

So putting the value in curve we get, $2 + \sqrt{4 + {\alpha}^{2}} = 4$

$⇒ 4 + {\alpha}^{2} = 16 + {\alpha}^{2} = 8\alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{3}{2}$

If $y = y\left(x\right)$, x \in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation

$2{e}^{- 4x}$\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)$,$ with $y$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ = {e}^{- \pi}$, then $y$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:

$2{e}^{- 4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)$

Now rewriting the given differential equation we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(8 + 4cot2x\right)y = \dfrac{2{e}^{- 4x}}{\sin^{2}2x}\left(2sinx + cos2x\right)$

Which is a linear differential equation.

$⇒ y\left({e}^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = ∫ 2{e}^{4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)dx$

$⇒ y\left({e}^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = {e}^{4x} \cdot sin2x + C$

So, the equation of curve is given by $y = \dfrac{{e}^{- 4x}}{sin2x}$

So, the value of $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{- 4\dfrac{\pi}{6}}}{sin\left(2 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}{e}^{- \dfrac{2\pi}{3}}$

questions.q: Let $y = {y}_{1}\left(x\right)$ and $y = {y}_{2}\left(x\right)$ be two distinct solutions of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y$, with ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 0$ and ${y}_{2}\left(0\right) = 1$ respectively. Then, the number of points of intersection of $y = {y}_{1}\left(x\right)$ and $y = {y}_{2}\left(x\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x$

So, $IF = {e}^{∫ - 1dx} = {e}^{- x}$

Now solution is given by $y{e}^{- x} = ∫ x{e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = - x{e}^{- x} - {e}^{- x} + c$

$⇒ y = - x - 1 + c{e}^{x}$

Given, ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 1$

$∴ {y}_{1} = - x - 1 + {e}^{x} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Also given ${y}_{2}\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 2$

$∴ {y}_{2} = - x - 1 + 2{e}^{x} ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right) we get, ${y}_{2} - {y}_{1} = {e}^{x} > 0 ∴ {y}_{2} \ne {y}_{1}$

$∴$ Number of points of intersection of ${y}_{1} and {y}_{2}$ is zero.

$

questions.q:
Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation
$sin\left(2{x}^{2}\right){\log}_{e}\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)dy + \left(4xy - 4\sqrt{2}xsin\left({x}^{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)dx = 0, 0 < x < \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$
, which passes through the point $\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}, 1\right)$. Then $\left|y\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\right)\right|$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given differential equation, $sin\left(2{x}^{2}\right)ln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)dy + \left(4xy - 4\sqrt{2}xsin\left({x}^{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ ln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)dy + \dfrac{4xydx}{sin\left(2{x}^{2}\right)} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}xsin\left({x}^{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}{sin\left(2{x}^{2}\right)}dx = 0$

$⇒ d\left(y \cdot ln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)\right) - 4\sqrt{2}x\dfrac{\left(sin{x}^{2} - cos{x}^{2}\right)}{\sqrt{2}\left(2sin{x}^{2}cos{x}^{2}\right)}dx = 0$

$⇒ d\left(yln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)\right) - \dfrac{4x\left(sin{x}^{2} - cos{x}^{2}\right)}{{\left(sin{x}^{2} + \cos^{2}x\right)}^{2} - 1}dx = 0$

Now integrating both side,

$⇒ ∫ d\left(yln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)\right) - ∫ \dfrac{4x\left(sin{x}^{2} - cos{x}^{2}\right)}{{\left(sin{x}^{2} + \cos^{2}x\right)}^{2} - 1}dx = ∫ 0$

Now let $sin{x}^{2} + \cos^{2}x = t ⇒ - 2x\left(sin{x}^{2} - \cos^{2}x\right) = dt$

$⇒ ∫ d\left(yln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right)\right) + 2 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{2} - 1} = ∫ 0$

$⇒ yln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right) + 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|\dfrac{t - 1}{t + 1}\right| = c$

$yln\left(tan{x}^{2}\right) + ln\left(\dfrac{sin{x}^{2} + cos{x}^{2} - 1}{sin{x}^{2} + cos{x}^{2} + 1}\right) = c$

Put y = 1 and $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}$

$1ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + ln\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 1\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 1\right)} = c$

Now at $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}$

$⇒ y\left(ln\sqrt{3}\right) + ln\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} - 1\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1\right)} = ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 3}\right)$

$⇒ y\left(ln\sqrt{3}\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)

$⇒ y = - 1$

So, \left|y\right| = 1$

questions.q: Let the solution curve $y = f\left(x\right)$ of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{xy}{{x}^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{{x}^{4} + 2x}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}, x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$ pass through the origin. Then ${∫}_{- \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}f\left(x\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{xy}{{x}^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{{x}^{4} + 2x}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$ is a linear differential equation.

Here $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{x}{{x}^{2} - 1}dx} = {e}^{\dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{2x}{{x}^{2} - 1}dx} = {e}^{\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)}$

i.e. $I . F . = \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}$\quad \because x \in(-1,1)$

So, solution of the differential equation is

$y \cdot \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{4} + 2x}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}} \cdot \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}dx$

$y\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} = ∫ \left({x}^{4} + 2x\right)dx$

$y\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} = \dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5} + {x}^{2} + C$

Since the curve passes through origin

so $x = 0, y = 0$⇒ C = 0$

i.e. $y = \dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$

Now,

${∫}_{\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}dx$

${∫}_{\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}f\left(x\right)dx = 0 + 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}dx$ (as $\dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$ is an odd function and$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$ is an even function)

Let $I = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}dx$

Assume $1 - {x}^{2} = {t}^{2} ⇒ 1 - {t}^{2} = {x}^{2}$

and $- 2tdt = 2xdx ⇒ dx = - \dfrac{tdt}{\sqrt{1 - {t}^{2}}}$

i.e. $I = ∫ \dfrac{1 - {t}^{2}}{t}\left(- \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{1 - {t}^{2}}}\right)dt$

$= - ∫ \sqrt{1 - {t}^{2}}dt$

$= - \left[\dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{1 - {t}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}t\right] + C$

$= - \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right] + C$

$⇒ {∫}_{\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}f\left(x\right)dx$

$= 2{\left[- \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$

$= 2\left(- \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}1\right)$

$= - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$

questions.q: Suppose $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution curve to the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2 - {e}^{- x}$ such that $\lim_{x \to \infty}y\left(x\right)$ is finite. If $a$ and $b$ are respectively the $x -$ and $y -$intercept of the tangent to the curve at $x = 0$, then the value of $a - 4b$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2 - {e}^{- x}$

Linear differential equation,

So, $I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ dx} = {e}^{- x}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times IF = ∫ \left(2 - {e}^{- x}\right) \times IFdx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = ∫ \left(2 - {e}^{- x}\right){e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = ∫ \left(2{e}^{- x} - {e}^{- 2x}\right)dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = - 2{e}^{- x} + \dfrac{{e}^{- 2x}}{2} + C$

$⇒ y = - 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2} + C{e}^{x}$

Given $\lim_{x \to \infty}y$ is finite

So, $\lim_{x \to \infty}\left(- 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2} + C \cdot {e}^{x}\right) \to$finite

This is possible only when $C = 0$

Hence$y = y\left(x\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2}$

Now finding the slope $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{- x}$

${\dfrac{dy}{dx}}_{x = 0} = - \dfrac{1}{2} = m, y\left(0\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

Now equation of tangent will be,

$y + \dfrac{3}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - 0\right)$

$⇒ x + 2y = - 3$

x-intercept $a = - 3,$ y-intercept $b = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

So, $a - 4b = - 3 + 6 = 3$

questions.solution:

So, the maximum value of $y\left(x\right)$ is $\dfrac{1}{8}$

If the curve passes through the points $\left(1, 2\right)$ and $\left(8, 1\right)$, then $\left|y\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} ∝ \dfrac{- y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- Ky}{x}$ (where $K$ is proportionality constant)

Now integrating both side,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} = - K ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|y\right| = - Kln\left|x\right| + C$

If the above equation satisfy $\left(1, 2\right)$

$⇒ ln2 = - K \times 0 + C ⇒ C = ln2$

So, $ln\left|y\right| = - Kln\left|x\right| + ln2$

Now it also passes through $\left(8, 1\right)$

$⇒ ln1 = - Kln8 + ln2 ⇒ K = \dfrac{1}{3}$

So, equation becomes $ln\left|y\right| = - \dfrac{1}{3}ln\left|x\right| + ln2$

So, at $x = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$⇒ ln\left|y\right| = - \dfrac{1}{3}ln\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right) + ln2 = 2ln2$

$⇒ \left|y\right| = 4$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4{y}^{3} + 2y{x}^{2}}{3x{y}^{2} + {x}^{3}}, y\left(1\right) = 1$. If for some $n \in N, y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$, then $n$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{\left(4{y}^{2} + 2{x}^{2}\right)}{\left(3{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}$

Let $y = vx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

So, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{\left(4{y}^{2} + 2{x}^{2}\right)}{\left(3{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v\left(4{v}^{2} + 2\right)}{\left(3{v}^{2} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v\left(\dfrac{\left(4{v}^{2} + 2 - 3{v}^{2} - 1\right)}{3{v}^{2} + 1}\right)$

$⇒ ∫ \left(3{v}^{2} + 1\right)\dfrac{dv}{{v}^{3} + v} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|{v}^{3} + v\right| = lnx + c$

$⇒ ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + c$

Given, $y\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ c = ln2$

So the equation becomes $ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + ln2$

Now for $y\left(2\right)$

So putting $x = 2$ in $ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + ln2$

We get, $ln\left(\dfrac{{y}^{3}}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2}\right) = 2ln2 ⇒ \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 4$

$⇒ \left[y\left(2\right)\right] = 2$

So, $y\left(2\right) \in [ 2, 3 )$

So on comparing with $y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$

$⇒ n = 3$

If $C$ passes through the points $\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$ and $\left(\alpha, \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{2\alpha}\right)$ then ${e}^{\alpha}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2{e}^{2x} - 6{e}^{- x} + 9}{2 + 9{e}^{- 2x}}$

On rearranging we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = {e}^{2x} - \dfrac{6{e}^{x}}{2{e}^{2x} + 9}$

Integrating both side we get,

$y = \dfrac{{e}^{2x}}{2} - \sqrt{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{x}}{3}\right) + c$

If the curve passes through the point $\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

Then $c = \sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

So, curve will be $y = \dfrac{{e}^{2x}}{2} - \sqrt{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{x}}{3}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

Again curve passes through the point

$\left(\alpha, \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{2\alpha}\right)$

Putting the value in curve equation we get,

$\dfrac{{e}^{2\alpha}}{2} = \dfrac{{e}^{2\alpha}}{2} - \sqrt{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\alpha}}{3}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\alpha}}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\alpha}}{3} = tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\alpha}}{3} = \left(\dfrac{tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} + {tantan}^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}{1 - tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} \times {tantan}^{- 1}\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{\alpha}}{3} = \left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}\right)$

$⇒ {e}^{\alpha} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{2}}{3 - \sqrt{2}}\right)$

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\left(x - {y}^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\left(x - {y}^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$

After rearranging we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{y}^{2} - x}{y\left(5x + {y}^{2}\right)}$

Now, let ${y}^{2} = v ⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\dfrac{1}{2y}\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v - x}{y\left(5x + v\right)}$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 2\left(\dfrac{v - x}{5x + v}\right)$

Now let $v = kx$

$⇒ k + x\dfrac{dk}{dx} = 2\left(\dfrac{kx - x}{5x + kx}\right)$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dk}{dx} = - \dfrac{\left({k}^{2} + 3k + 2\right)}{k + 5}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{\left(5 + k\right)}{\left(k + 1\right)\left(k + 2\right)}dk = ∫ - \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{4}{k + 1} - \dfrac{3}{k + 2}\right)dk = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ 4ln\left(k + 1\right) - 3ln\left(k + 2\right) = - lnx + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(k + 1\right)}^{4}}{{\left(k + 2\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 1\right)}^{4}}{{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 2\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ c{\left({y}^{2} + 2x\right)}^{3} = {\left({y}^{2} + x\right)}^{4}$

If $y\left(3\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{\alpha} + 1}{\beta{e}^{\alpha}}$. then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given, $\left(x - 1\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2xy = \dfrac{1}{x - 1}$

$I . F = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2x}{x - 1}} = {e}^{2x} \times {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}$

Solution will be,

$y = \dfrac{1}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}}\left[\dfrac{{e}^{2x} + 1}{2{e}^{2x}}\right]$

questions.solution:
Given,

$x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = \sqrt{{y}^{2} + 16{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{y}^{2} + 16{x}^{2}} + y}{x}$

Let $y = xt ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\dfrac{dt}{dx} + t$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} + t = t + \sqrt{{t}^{2} + 16}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 16}} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 16}} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|t + \sqrt{{t}^{2} + 16}\right| = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{\sqrt{{y}^{2} + 16{x}^{2}}}{x} = cx$

$∵ y\left(1\right) = 3$ so $⇒ \dfrac{3}{1} + \dfrac{\sqrt{{3}^{2} + 16 \times {1}^{2}}}{1} = c \times 1 ⇒ c = 8$

So solution becomes,

$\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{\sqrt{{y}^{2} + 16{x}^{2}}}{x} = 8x$

Now $y\left(2\right) = \dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{{y}^{2} + 16 \times {2}^{2}}}{2} = 8 \times 2$

$⇒ y + \sqrt{{y}^{2} + 64} = 32$

$⇒ y = 15$

If $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\left(\alpha\right)}$, then the value of $3{\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x}y = x{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

$= 2\sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}2xdx}{2 + \tan^{2}2x}$

Put $tan2x = t$

$I = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{tan2x}{\sqrt{2}}$

$∴ IF = {e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{tan2x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} = {e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

So general solution will be

$y{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = ∫ x{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}dx$

$y{e}^{{cot}^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = e\dfrac{\pi}{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) + c$

$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{32} ⇒ c = 0$

i.e. $y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

Given $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha} = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$= \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{18}{e}^{- \tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)}$

Hence $\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} ⇒ 3{\alpha}^{2} = 2$

Divide by ${y}^{3}$

$2e\dfrac{x}{{y}^{2}} + lny + c = 0$

questions.solution:
Given $x\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3{x}^{2}y - y - 4{x}^{3}\right) = 0$

$\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right)y = 4{x}^{3}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\left(3{x}^{2} - 1\right)}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}y = \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$

Here $IF = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{3{x}^{2} - 1}{x - {x}^{3}}dx}$

Let $x - {x}^{3} = t ⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{dt}{t}}$

$= {e}^{- lnt} = \dfrac{1}{t}$

$∴ IF = \dfrac{1}{x - {x}^{3}}$

So the general solution of the differential equation will be

$y \times IF = ∫ Q \times IFdx$

$y\left(\dfrac{1}{x - {x}^{3}}\right) = ∫ \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{x - {x}^{3}} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4{x}^{3}}{{\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)}^{2}}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4x}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Now let $I = ∫ \dfrac{4x}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Substituting $1 - {x}^{2} = z$

$I = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- dz}{{z}^{2}}$

$= - 2\left(- \dfrac{1}{z}\right) + c = \dfrac{2}{1 - {x}^{2}} + c$

Hence the solution of the differential equation becomes

$\dfrac{y}{x - {x}^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{1 - {x}^{2}} + c$

At $x = 2, y = - 2$

Here $IF = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{3{x}^{2} - 1}{x - {x}^{3}}dx}$

questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation $\left(\left(\tan^{- 1}y\right) - x\right)dy = \left(1 + {y}^{2}\right)dx$ passes through the point $\left(1, 0\right)$ then the abscissa of the point on the curve whose ordinate is $tan \left(1\right) is$
questions.solution:
$\left(\tan^{- 1}y - x\right)dy = \left(1 + {y}^{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{1}{1 + {y}^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{\tan^{- 1}y}{1 + {y}^{2}}$

I.F. $= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + {y}^{2}}dy} = {e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}$

General solution will be

$x\left({e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = ∫ {e}^{\tan^{- 1}y} \times \dfrac{\tan^{- 1}y}{1 + {y}^{2}}dy$

$⇒ x\left({e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = \tan^{- 1}y\left({e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) - {e}^{\tan^{- 1}y} + C$

Since the curve passes through $\left(1, 0\right) ⇒ C = 2$

So, the curve reduces to $x\left({e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = \tan^{- 1}y\left({e}^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) - {e}^{\tan^{- 1}y} + 2$

when $y = tan1, x\left(e\right) = 1\left(e\right) - e + 2$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{e}$

its passes through $\left(2, 5\right)$

so circle will be ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2x - 2y - 23 = 0$

centre $C = \left(- 1, 1\right)

and radius $5$

questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{{2}^{x - y}\left({2}^{y} - 1\right)}{{2}^{x} - 1} = 0$x, y > 0, y\left(1\right) = 1$

Now rearranging and integrating both side of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{{2}^{x}\left({2}^{y} - 1\right)}{{2}^{y}\left({2}^{x} - 1\right)}$, we get

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{y}}{{2}^{y} - 1}dy = - ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{x}}{{2}^{x} - 1}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ln2} ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{y}ln2}{{2}^{y} - 1}dy = - \dfrac{1}{\ln^{2}} ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{x}ln2}{{2}^{x} - 1}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ln2}ln\left|{2}^{y} - 1\right| = \dfrac{- 1}{ln2}ln\left|{2}^{x} - 1\right| + C$

At $x = 1, y = 1$

Putting this values in above equation we get $C = 0$

So, $ln\left|{2}^{y} - 1\right| + ln\left|{2}^{x} - 1\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left({2}^{x} - 1\right)\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = 1$

$⇒ {2}^{y} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{x} + 1}$

At $x = 2$

$⇒ {2}^{y} = \dfrac{1}{3} + 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$y = {\log}_{2}\dfrac{4}{3} = {\log}_{2}4 - {\log}_{2}3 = 2 - {\log}_{2}3$

questions.q: If $y = y\left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = x{e}^{x}, y\left(1\right) = 0$ then the local maximum value of the function $z\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}y ( x ) - {e}^{x}, x \in R$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2y}{x} = {e}^{x}$

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = {e}^{2lnx} = {x}^{2}$

$∴$ General solution: $y\left({x}^{2}\right) = ∫ {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2}\right)dx$

We know that

$∫ {e}^{x}f\left(x\right)dx = = {e}^{x}\left[f\left(x\right) - {f}^{'} ( x ) + {f}^{''}\left(x\right) - {f}^{'''}\left(x\right)\left+ ⋯ + {\left(- 1\right)}^{n}{f}^{n}\left(x\right)\right)\right] + C$

So, $y\left({x}^{2}\right) = {e}^{x}\left[{x}^{2} - 2x + 2\right] + C . . . \left(i\right)$

Given $y\left(1\right) = 0 ⇒ \left(0\right)\left(1\right) = {e}^{1}\left[1 - 2\left(1\right) + 2\right] + C$

$⇒ C = - e$

$∴ y = \dfrac{{e}^{x}}{{x}^{2}}\left[{x}^{2} - 2x + 2\right] - e$ (from eq $\left(i\right)$)

Hence, $z ( x ) = {x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{e}^{x}}{{x}^{2}}\right)\left[{x}^{2} - 2x + 2\right] - e - {e}^{x}$

$= {e}^{x}\left[{x}^{2} - 2x + 2\right] - e - {e}^{x}$

$z\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left[{x}^{2} - 2x + 1\right] - e$

${z}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x - 2\right) + \left({x}^{2} - 2x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

${z}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left[{x}^{2} - 1\right]$
To find local maxima, put ${z}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) = 0 ⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(x + 1\right) = 0 \left(∵ {e}^{x} > 0, ∀ x \in R\right)$

$⇒ x = 1, - 1$

It is clear from the sign scheme method, $z\left(x\right) has local maximum value at $x = - 1$ and has local minimum value at $x = 1$.

$∴$ The local maximum value is

$z$\left(- 1\right)$ = {e}^{- 1}$\left[{\left(- 1\right)$}^{2} - 2$\left(- 1\right) + 1\right] - e$

$= \dfrac{1}{e}\left[1 + 2 + 1\right]$ - e = $\dfrac{4}{e} -$e$

$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)y = \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$ and $y\left(0\right) = 0$, then the value of $y\left(2\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)y = \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$

It is linear differential equation so,

$IF = {e}^{∫ \left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{x}dx}$

$= {e}^{{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - 2 ∫ x{e}^{x}dx - 2{e}^{x}} = {e}^{{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - 2\left[x{e}^{x} - {e}^{x}\right] - 2{e}^{x}}$

$IF = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}$

Now solution is given by

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = ∫ {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} \times \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$

$= ∫ {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} \times \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{x}$

Now let $\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} = t$

We get ${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right) + {e}^{x}\left(2x - 2\right)dx = dt$

${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2x + 2x - 2\right)dx = dt$

${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)dx = dt$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = ∫ {e}^{t} \times t \times dt$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{t}\left(t - 1\right) + c$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}\left(\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} - 1\right) + c$

Now at $x = 0y = 0$

$0 \times {e}^{0} = {e}^{0}\left(0x{e}^{x} - 1\right) + c$

$0 = - 1 + c c = 1$

Putting the value of $c = 1$ we get the equation as

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}\left(\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} - 1\right) + 1$

Now putting $x = 2$ in equation we get

$y \times {e}^{\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2}} = {e}^{\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2}}\left(\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{0} = {e}^{0}\left(\left(0\right){e}^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y = - 1 + 1 = 0$

Given $\left(4 + {x}^{2}\right)dy - 2x\left({x}^{2} + 3y + 4\right)dx = 0$

$\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2{x}^{3} + 6xy + 8x$

$\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 6xy = 2{x}^{3} + 8x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{6x}{{x}^{2} + 4}y = \dfrac{2{x}^{3} + 8x}{{x}^{2} + 4}$

This is of the form of linear differential equation

I.F. $= {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{6x}{{x}^{2} + 4}dx} = {e}^{- 3{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}$

$= {e}^{{\log}_{e}{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{1}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}}$

So the solution of the differential equation will be

$y . \dfrac{1}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}} = ∫ \dfrac{2{x}^{3} + 8x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}dx$

$\dfrac{y}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}} = ∫ \dfrac{2x\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}dx$

Let ${x}^{2} + 4 = t$, $2xdx = dt$

So $\dfrac{y}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}} = ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{3}}$

$\dfrac{y}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{- 1}{2{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{2}} + C$

Since the curve passes through origin $\left(0, 0\right)$

$0 = \dfrac{- 1}{2 \times 16} + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{32}$

i.e. $\dfrac{y}{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}} = \dfrac{- 1}{2{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{32}$

$y = \dfrac{- \left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}{2} + \dfrac{{\left({x}^{2} + 4\right)}^{3}}{32}$

Hence $y\left(2\right) = - \dfrac{8}{2} + \dfrac{8 \times 8 \times 8}{32} = 12$

questions.q: Let $S = \left(0, 2\pi\right) - \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right\}$. Let $y = y\left(x\right)$, $x \in S$, be the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x}, y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$. If the sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection of the curve $y = y\left(x\right)$ with the curve $y = \sqrt{2}sinx$ is $\dfrac{k\pi}{12}$, then $k$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left(sinx + cosx\right)}^{2}}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + tanx\right)}^{2}}$

$y = - \dfrac{1}{1 + tanx} + C$

So $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So $\dfrac{1}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2} + C$⇒ C = 1$

So $y = \dfrac{- 1}{1 + tanx} + 1$

$y = \dfrac{- 1 + 1 + tanx}{1 + tanx}$

$y = \dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx}$

Solving this equation with $y = \sqrt{2}sinx$

$\dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx} = \sqrt{2}sinx$

i.e. $sinx = 0, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = sinx + cosx$

$x = \pi$

or $\dfrac{1}{2} = sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6}, 2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}, x = \dfrac{13\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$x = \dfrac{7\pi}{12}, x = \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

Hence sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection

$= \pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

$= \dfrac{12\pi + 7\pi + 23}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12}$

$\dfrac{k\pi}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12} ⇒ k = 42$

$⇒ \dfrac{- dv}{1 + {v}^{2}} = \dfrac{dy}{y}$

Now Integrating Both side

$⇒ - ∫ \dfrac{dy}{1 + {v}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y}$

$⇒ - \tan^{- 1}v = log\left|y\right| + c$⇒ - \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = log\left|y\right| + c$

Also this curve passes through $\left(1, 1\right)$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}1 = log\left|1\right| + c$⇒ c = - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$⇒ - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{y} = log\left|y\right| - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Now putting $y = \sqrt{3}x$ and $x = \alpha$ we get

$= - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}x} = log\left|\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$= - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = log\left(\sqrt{3}\alpha\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$= - \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = log\left|\sqrt{3}\alpha\right|$

$⇒ log\left|\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

Let surface area of the spherical balloon A = 4\pi{r}^{2}$

\dfrac{dA}{dt} =$8\pir$\dfrac{dr}{dt} =k$ (let) $. . . \left(1\right)

On integrating on both sides w.r.t $t$ , we get

Given that, at $t = 0, r = 3$.

$⇒ 36\pi = C$

Also given that, at $t = 5, r = 7$

$⇒ 4\pi \times 49 = 5k + 36\pi$

$⇒ 5k = 4\pi $\left(49 - 9\right)$ ⇒ 5k = 4\pi \times 40$

$⇒ k = 32\pi$

$⇒ {r}^{2} = 8t + 9$

Given $t = 9$.

$⇒ {r}^{2} = 81 ⇒ r = 9$.

$

questions.q: If $y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\left[\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)}{{ϕ}^{'}\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)}\right], x > 0, ϕ > 0,$ and $y ( 1 ) = - 1,$ then $ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:$\dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left[\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)}{{ϕ}^{'}\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)}\right] . . . . \left(1\right)$

Let $\dfrac{y}{x} = t$

$⇒ y = xt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = t + x \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$∴ t\left(t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}\right) = \left({t}^{2} + \dfrac{ϕ\left({t}^{2}\right)}{{ϕ}^{'}\left({t}^{2}\right)}\right)$

$⇒ xt\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{ϕ\left({t}^{2}\right)}{ϕ ' \left({t}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{t \cdot {ϕ}^{'}\left({t}^{2}\right)}{ϕ\left({t}^{2}\right)}dt = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$
Integrating both sides

$∫ \dfrac{t \cdot {ϕ}^{'}\left({t}^{2}\right)}{ϕ\left({t}^{2}\right)}dt = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

Let $ϕ\left({t}^{2}\right) = p$

$⇒ {ϕ}^{'}\left({t}^{2}\right) . 2t = dp$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{1}{p}dp = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}lnp = lnx + C$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}lnϕ\left({t}^{2}\right) = lnx + C$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)\right) = lnx + C . . . \left(2\right)$

If $x = 1, y = - 1$ then $C = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(ϕ\left(1\right)\right)$

Substituting value of $C$ in $\left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)\right) = lnx + \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(ϕ\left(1\right)\right)$

$⇒$ln\left(ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\right)\right) = ln{x}^{2} + ln\left(ϕ\left(1\right)\right)$

If $x = 2$ then

$ln\left(ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4}\right)\right) = ln4 + ln\left(ϕ\left(1\right)\right)$

SO, $ϕ\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{4}\right) = 4ϕ\left(1\right)$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}y + {2}^{y} \cdot {2}^{x}}{{2}^{x} + {2}^{x + y}{\log}_{e}2}, y\left(0\right) = 0,$ then for $y = 1,$ the value of $x$ lies in the interval :
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x} \cdot y + {2}^{y} \cdot {2}^{x}}{{2}^{x} + {2}^{x + y}{\log}_{e}2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}\left(y + {2}^{y}\right)}{{2}^{x}\left(1 + {2}^{y}{\log}_{e}2\right)}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{1 + {2}^{y}{\log}_{e}2}{y + {2}^{y}}dy = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(y + {2}^{y}\right)}{y + {2}^{y}} = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ln\left|y + {2}^{y}\right| = x + C\left[∵ ∫ \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}dx = ln\left(f\left(x\right)\right) + C\right]$

Now $∵ y\left(0\right) = 0$

$⇒ C = 0$

$∴ ln\left|y + {2}^{y}\right| = x$

Now for $y = 1$ we have

$x = ln\left(1 + 2\right) = ln3 \in \left(1, 2\right)$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{{2}^{y}}, y\left(0\right) = 1,$ then $y ( 1 )$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given that

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{{2}^{y}} = {2}^{x}\left(\dfrac{{2}^{y} - 1}{{2}^{y}}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{2}^{y}}{{2}^{y} - 1}\right)dy = {2}^{x}dx$

By using Variable Separable method

$∫ \dfrac{{2}^{y}dy}{{2}^{y} - 1} = ∫ {2}^{x}dx$

Let ${2}^{y} - 1 = t ⇒ {2}^{y}ln\left(2\right)dy = dt$

$∫ \dfrac{dt}{t}\dfrac{1}{ℓn2} = ∫ {2}^{x}dx$

We know that $∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx = ln\left(x\right) + c \text{ and } ∫ {a}^{x}dx = \dfrac{{a}^{x}}{ln\left(a\right)} + c .$

$⇒ \dfrac{ln\left(t\right)}{ln\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{{2}^{x}}{ln\left(2\right)} + \dfrac{c}{ln\left(2\right)}$

$⇒ ln\left(t\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

$⇒ ln\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

when $x = 0, y = 1 ⇒ ln\left(2 - 1\right) = {2}^{0} + c$

$⇒ c = - 1 .$

$⇒ ln\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = {2}^{x} - 1$

$⇒ {2}^{y} - 1 = {e}^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

$⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + {e}^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

when $x = 1 ⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + {e}^{1} ⇒ y = {\log}_{2} ( 1 + e )$

questions.q: A differential equation representing the family of parabolas with axis parallel to $y -$axis and whose length of latus rectum is the distance of the point $( 2, - 3 )$ from the line $3x + 4y = 5$, is given by:
questions.solution:
The equation of family of parabolas

$( x - \alpha{)}^{2} = 4a ( y - \beta )$
Distance of point $( 2, - 3 )$ from line $3x + 4y = 5$ is
$4a = \left|\dfrac{3 \times 2 + 4 \times \left(- 3\right) - 5}{5}\right|$

$4a = \left|\dfrac{6 - 12 - 5}{5}\right|$

$4a = \dfrac{11}{5}$

$( x - \alpha{)}^{2} = \dfrac{11}{5} ( y - \beta )$
Differentiate w.r.t. $x$
$2 ( x - \alpha ) = \dfrac{11}{5}\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Again diff. w. r. t. $x$

$2 = \dfrac{11}{5}\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$

$11\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = 10$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be a solution curve of the differential equation $\left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}xdx + tanxdy + ydx = 0$, $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. If $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}xy\left(x\right) = 1$, then the value of $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
Given:

$\left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}xdx + tanxdy + ydx = 0$

$⇒ \left[\left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}x + y\right]dx + tanxdy = 0$

$⇒ tanx\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) + \left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}x + y = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(1 + y\right)tanx = - ycotx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(tanx + cotx\right) = - tanx$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P\left(x\right)y = Q\left(x\right)$.

$\text{I.F} = {e}^{∫ ( tanx + cotx ) dx}$

$= {e}^{∫ \left(\dfrac{\tan^{2}x + 1}{tanx}\right)dx}$

$= {e}^{∫ \left(\dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{tanx}\right)dx}$

$= {e}^{{\log}_{e}\left|tanx\right|}$

$= tanx\left(∵ x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)$

Solution is

$ytanx = ∫ - \tan^{2}xdx + c$

$⇒ ytanx = ∫ \left(1 - {sec}^{2}x\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ytanx = x - tanx + c$

Now,

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}xy = 1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\left(\dfrac{x}{tanx}\right)\left(x - tanx + c\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 ( 0 - 0 + c ) = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

Then the function is

$ytanx = x - tanx + 1$

Put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$,

$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + 1$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Solution is

$ytanx = ∫ - \tan^{2}xdx + c$

$⇒ ytanx = x - tanx + c$

Now,

$\left(x - {x}^{3}\right)dy = \left(y + y{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4}\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy - ydx = \left(y{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4}\right)dx + {x}^{3}dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = ( ydx + xdy ) - 3{x}^{2}dx$

$⇒ d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = d\left(xy\right) - d\left({x}^{3}\right)$

Integrate

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = xy - {x}^{3} + c$

given $f\left(3\right) = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{3} = 3 \times 3 - {3}^{3} + c$

$⇒ c = 19$

$∴ \dfrac{y}{x} = xy - {x}^{3} + 19$

at $x = 4, \dfrac{y}{4} = 4y - 64 + 19$

$15y = 4 \times 45$

$⇒ y = 12$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $dy = {e}^{\alphax + y}dx; \alpha \in N .$ If $y\left({\log}_{e}2\right) = {\log}_{e}2$ and $y\left(0\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right),$ then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to ___.
questions.solution:
We have, $∫ {e}^{- y}dy = ∫ {e}^{\alphax}dx$

$⇒ - {e}^{- y} = \dfrac{{e}^{\alphax}}{\alpha} + c . . . \left(1\right)$

Put $\left(x, y\right) = \left(ℓn2, ℓn2\right)$

$- \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{{2}^{\alpha}}{\alpha} + c . . . \left(2\right)$

Put $\left(x, y\right) ≡ \left(0, - ℓn2\right)$

$- 2 = \dfrac{1}{\alpha} + c$

From equation $\left(1\right) - \left(2\right),$ we get

$\dfrac{{2}^{\alpha} - 1}{\alpha} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 2 ($ as $\alpha \in N )$.

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be solution of the differential equation ${\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 3x + 4y,$ with $y\left(0\right) = 0$. If $y\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right) = \alpha{\log}_{e}2$, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given,

${\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 3x + 4y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = {e}^{3x} \cdot {e}^{4y}$

$⇒ ∫ {e}^{- 4y}dy = ∫ {e}^{3x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{{e}^{- 4y}}{- 4} = \dfrac{{e}^{3x}}{3} + C$

Given,

$y\left(0\right) = 0$

So,

$- \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{3} = C ⇒ C = - \dfrac{7}{12}$

So, the particular solution is

$\dfrac{{e}^{- 4y}}{- 4} = \dfrac{{e}^{3x}}{3} - \dfrac{7}{12}$

$⇒ {e}^{- 4y} = \dfrac{4{e}^{3x} - 7}{- 3}$

$⇒ {e}^{4y} = \dfrac{3}{7 - 4{e}^{3x}} ⇒ 4y = ln\left(\dfrac{3}{7 - 4{e}^{3x}}\right)$

$4y = ℓn\left(\dfrac{3}{6}\right)$ when $x = - \dfrac{2}{3}ℓn2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{4}ℓn\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = - \dfrac{1}{4}ℓn2$

So, $\alpha = - \dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.q: If $y = y\left(x\right), y \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation $secy\dfrac{dy}{dx} - sin\left(x + y\right) - sin\left(x - y\right) = 0,$ with $y\left(0\right) = 0$, then $5{y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$secy\dfrac{dy}{dx} - sin\left(x + y\right) - sin\left(x - y\right) = 0$

$⇒ secy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2sinxcosy$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}ydy = 2sinxdx$

$⇒ ∫ {sec}^{2}ydy = ∫ 2sinxdx$

$⇒ tany = - 2cosx + c$

Given, $y\left(0\right) = 0$

So, $0 = - 2cos0 + c$

$⇒ c = 2$

So, the particular solution is

$tany = - 2cosx + 2$

at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, tany = - 2cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2$

$⇒ tany = 2 ⇒ {sec}^{2}y = 5$

Here, differentiate both sides of $tany = - 2cosx + 2,$ we get,

${sec}^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2sinx$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$5\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ 5\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $xdy = \left(y + {x}^{3}cosx\right)dx$ with $y\left(\pi\right) = 0,$ then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
We have, $xdy = \left(y + {x}^{3}cosx\right)dx$

$⇒ xdy = ydx + {x}^{3}cosxdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{{x}^{3}cosxdx}{{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = ∫ xcosxdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx - ∫ 1 . sinxdx$

Therefore, $\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + C$

At $x = \pi, y = 0,$

$0 = - 1 + C$

$⇒ C = 1, x = \pi, y = 0$

So, $\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + 1$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2}sinx + xcosx + x$

Hence, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + x{e}^{y - x}, - \sqrt{2} < x < \sqrt{2}, y\left(0\right) = 0$, then the minimum value of $y\left(x\right), x \in \left(- \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + x{e}^{y - x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy - dx}{{e}^{y - x}} = xdx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(y - x\right)}{{e}^{y - x}} = ∫ xdx$

$⇒ - {e}^{x - y} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + c$

At $x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ c = - 1$

So, the particular solution is

${e}^{x - y} = \dfrac{2 - {x}^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ y = x - ln\left(\dfrac{2 - {x}^{2}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \dfrac{2x}{2 - {x}^{2}} = \dfrac{2 + 2x - {x}^{2}}{2 - {x}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{x}^{2} - 2x - 2}{{x}^{2} - 2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{x}^{2} - 2x - 2}{\left(x + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(x - \sqrt{2}\right)}$

If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 ⇒ {x}^{2} - 2x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2}$

$⇒ x = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}$

So minimum value occurs at $x = 1 - \sqrt{3}$

$y\left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right) = \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right) - ln\left(\dfrac{2 - ( 4 - 2\sqrt{3} )}{2}\right)$

$= \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right) - ln\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right)$

questions.q:
Let $y = y ( x )$ be solution of the following differential equation

${e}^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2{e}^{y}sinx + sinx\cos^{2}x = 0, y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$.

If $y\left(0\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\alpha + \beta{e}^{- 2}\right)$, then $4 ( \alpha + \beta )$ is equal to .
questions.solution:
Let ${e}^{y} = t ⇒ {e}^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

So,

${e}^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2{e}^{y}sinx + sinx\cos^{2}x = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} - \left(2sinx\right)t = - sinx\cos^{2}x$

So, the integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ - 2sinxdx} = {e}^{2cosx}$

So, the solution of differential equation is

$t \cdot {e}^{2cosx} = ∫ {e}^{2cosx} \cdot \left(- sinx\cos^{2}x\right)dx$

$⇒ {e}^{y} \cdot {e}^{2cosx} = ∫ {e}^{2z} \cdot {z}^{2}dz$ (Assume, $z = cosx ⇒ dz = - sinx$)

Using integration by parts,

$⇒ {e}^{y} \cdot {e}^{2cosx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot {z}^{2} \cdot {e}^{2z} - \dfrac{1}{2}z \cdot {e}^{2z} + \dfrac{{e}^{2z}}{4} + C$

$⇒ {e}^{y} \cdot {e}^{2cosx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \cos^{2}x \cdot {e}^{2cosx} - \dfrac{1}{2}cosx \cdot {e}^{2cosx} + \dfrac{{e}^{2cosx}}{4} + C$

at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, y = 0 ⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ {e}^{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{2}x - \dfrac{1}{2}cosx + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot {e}^{- 2cosx}$

Put $x = 0$

$⇒ y = log\left[\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}{e}^{- 2}\right] ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{4}, \beta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

So, $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} = 1$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx,$ with $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0 .$ Then, the value of ${\left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{\sin^{2}x} + 2dx = \left(\dfrac{1 + ycos2x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x = 1 + ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x - 1 = ycos2x$

Using, $cos2x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x,$ we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right) = ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right)y = cos2x$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P \text{ and } Q$ are the functions of $x$ or constants.

Thus, $P = - cos2x \text{ and } Q = cos2x$

Now, we have integrating factor I.F.$= {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ - cos2xdx} = {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}$

And, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ \left(cos2x\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}dx + c$

Put $\dfrac{sin2x}{2} = t, ⇒ \dfrac{2cos2x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + c$

Given, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 0 \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} + c$

$⇒ c = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, at $x = 0$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{0} = - {e}^{0} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) = - 1 + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) + 1 = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ {\left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)}^{2} = {e}^{- 1} .$

Now, we have integrating factor I.F.$= {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ - cos2xdx} = {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}$

And, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ \left(cos2x\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}dx + c$

Put $\dfrac{sin2x}{2} = t, ⇒ \dfrac{2cos2x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + c$

Given, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 0 \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} + c$

$⇒ c = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, at $x = 0$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{0} = - {e}^{0} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) = - 1 + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) + 1 = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ {\left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)}^{2} = {e}^{- 1} .$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(\left(x + 2\right){e}^{\left(\dfrac{y + 1}{x + 2}\right)} + \left(y + 1\right)\right)dx = \left(x + 2\right)dy, y\left(1\right) = 1 .$ If the domain of $y = y\left(x\right)$ is an open interval $( \alpha, \beta ) ,$ then $| \alpha + \beta |$ is equal to ___________.
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\left(\left(x + 2\right){e}^{\left(\dfrac{y + 1}{x + 2}\right)} + \left(y + 1\right)\right)dx = \left(x + 2\right)dy, y\left(1\right) = 1$

Let, $y + 1 = Y ⇒ dy = dY$ and $x + 2 = X ⇒ dx = dX$ and at $y = 1, Y = 2$ and at $x = 1, X = 3 .$

Thus, the differential equation becomes $\left(Xe\dfrac{Y}{X} + Y\right)dX = XdY$

$⇒ XdY - YdX = Xe\dfrac{Y}{X}dX$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(XdY - YdX\right)}{{X}^{2}} = \left(\dfrac{X{e}^{\dfrac{Y}{X}}}{{X}^{2}}\right)dX$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dX}\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right) = \left(\dfrac{X{e}^{\dfrac{Y}{X}}}{{X}^{2}}\right)dX$

$⇒ d\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right){e}^{- \dfrac{Y}{X}} = \dfrac{dX}{X}$

Integrating both sides w.r.to $X,$ we get $∫ d\left(\dfrac{Y}{X}\right){e}^{- \dfrac{Y}{X}} = ∫ \dfrac{dX}{X}$

$⇒ - {e}^{- \dfrac{Y}{X}} = {\log}_{e}\left|X\right| + c$

Given, at $X = 3, Y = 2$

$⇒ - {e}^{- \dfrac{2}{3}} = {\log}_{e}\left|3\right| + c$

$⇒ c = - {e}^{- \dfrac{2}{3}} - {\log}_{e}\left|3\right|$

$⇒ - {e}^{- \dfrac{Y}{X}} = {\log}_{e}\left|X\right| - {e}^{- \dfrac{2}{3}} - {\log}_{e}3$

${e}^{- \dfrac{Y}{X}} = e\dfrac{2}{3} + {\log}_{e}3 - {\log}_{e}\left|X\right| > 0$

${\log}_{e}\left|X\right| < e\dfrac{2}{3} + {\log}_{e}3$

Let, $\lambda = \left(e\dfrac{2}{3} + {\log}_{e}3\right)$ then, we have $\left|x + 2\right| < {e}^{\lambda}$

$⇒ - {e}^{\lambda} < x + 2 < {e}^{\lambda}$

$⇒ - {e}^{\lambda} - 2 < x < {e}^{\lambda} - 2$

Thus, the domain of the function is $\left(- {e}^{\lambda} - 2, {e}^{\lambda} - 2\right) .$

Given, the domain of the function is $\left(\alpha, \beta\right),$ hence $\alpha = - {e}^{\lambda} - 2 \text{ and } \beta = {e}^{\lambda} - 2$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = - {e}^{\lambda} - 2 + {e}^{\lambda} - 2 = - 4$

$⇒ | \alpha + \beta | = 4 .$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ satisfies the equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \left|A\right| = 0,$ for all $x > 0,$ where $A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$. If $y ( \pi ) = \pi + 2,$ then the value of $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
We have,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

Now,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left|A\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = 2sinx + 2$

$\text{I.F.} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = x$

Solution is

$y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(I . F .\right) \times \left(2sinx + 2\right)dx$

$⇒ yx = ∫ x ( 2sinx + 2 ) dx$

$⇒ yx = 2 ∫ x\left(sinx\right)dx + 2 ∫ xdx$

$⇒ xy = {x}^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx + c \ldots \left(i\right)$

Now $x = \pi, y = \pi + 2$, hence

$⇒ \pi\left(\pi + 2\right) = {\pi}^{2} - 2\pi\left(- 1\right) + 0 + c$

$⇒ c = 0$

Now $\left(i\right)$ becomes

$xy = {x}^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx$

Put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then

$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)y = {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2} - 2 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)y = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} + 2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{4}{\pi}$

questions.q: Let a curve $y = y \left(x\right) be given by$ the solution of the differential equationcos $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1}\left({e}^{- x}\right)\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{{e}^{2x} - 1}\right)dy$. If it intersects $y$-axis at $y = - 1$, and the intersection point of the curve with $x -$axis is $\left(\alpha, 0\right)$, then ${e}^{\alpha}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,

$cos\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1}\left({e}^{- x}\right)\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{{e}^{2x} - 1}\right)dy . . . \left(i\right)$

Put $\cos^{- 1}\left({e}^{- x}\right) = \theta, \theta \in \left[0, \pi\right]$

$⇒ cos\theta = {e}^{- x}$

$⇒ 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2} - 1 = {e}^{- x}$

$⇒ cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{{e}^{- x} + 1}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{e}^{x} + 1}{2{e}^{x}}}$

Hence, by $\left(i\right)$, we have

$cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{{e}^{2x} - 1}\right)dy$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{{e}^{x} + 1}{2{e}^{x}}}dx = \sqrt{{e}^{2x} - 1}dy$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{{e}^{x} + 1}{2{e}^{x}}}\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{{e}^{x} - 1}\right)\left(\sqrt{{e}^{x} + 1}\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{{e}^{x}}\sqrt{{e}^{x} - 1}} = ∫ dy$

Put ${e}^{x} = t ⇒ dt = {e}^{x}dx$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{e}^{x}\sqrt{{e}^{x}}\sqrt{{e}^{x} - 1}} = ∫ dy$

$∫ \dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{{t}^{2} - t}} = \sqrt{2} ∫ dy$

Put $t = \dfrac{1}{z} ⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dz} = - \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}$

$∫ \dfrac{- \dfrac{dz}{{z}^{2}}}{\dfrac{1}{z}\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{z}}} = \sqrt{2} ∫ dy$

$⇒ - ∫ \dfrac{dz}{\sqrt{1 - z}} = \sqrt{2} ∫ dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2 ( 1 - z{)}^{1 / 2}}{- 1} = \sqrt{2}y + c$

$⇒ 2{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{1 / 2} = \sqrt{2}y + c$

$⇒ 2{\left(1 - {e}^{- x}\right)}^{1 / 2} = \sqrt{2}y + c$

Now, it meets $y - \text{axis}$ at $\left(0, - 1\right)$, hence

$0 = - \sqrt{2} + c ⇒ c = \sqrt{2}$

Hence,

$2{\left(1 - {e}^{- x}\right)}^{1 / 2} = \sqrt{2}\left(y + 1\right)$

It passes through $\left(\alpha, 0\right)$

$2{\left(1 - {e}^{- \alpha}\right)}^{1 / 2} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - {e}^{- \alpha}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ 1 - {e}^{- \alpha} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {e}^{- \alpha} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ {e}^{\alpha} = 2$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $xtan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = \left(ytan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - x\right)dx$, $- 1 \le x \le 1, y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6} .$ Then the area of the region bounded by the curves $x = 0, x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $y = y\left(x\right)$ in the upper half plane is:
questions.solution:
We have,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{y}{x} \cdot tan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - 1\right)}{xtan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} - cot\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$

Put $y = vx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\left(\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)$

Now, we get

$v + x\left(\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = v - cotv$

$⇒ ∫ tanvdv = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|secv\right| = - ln\left|x\right| + c$

$⇒ ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = - ln\left|x\right| + c$

$⇒ ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| + ln\left|x\right| = c$

Now, $y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, then

$ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right| + ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = c$

$⇒ ln2 + ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = c$

$⇒ ln2 - ln2 = c$

$⇒ c = 0$

Hence,

$∴ sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = x$

$⇒ y = x\cos^{- 1}\left(x\right)$

So, required bounded area

$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\cos^{- 1}x}_{⏟}}_{I}\right)\mathop{x}_{II}dx$

$= {\left[\cos^{- 1}x \cdot \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} + \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\dfrac{1 - {x}^{2} - 1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}x - \sin^{- 1}x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\right]$

$= \left(\dfrac{\pi - 1}{8}\right)$ sq. units

Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation ${e}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}dx + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = 0, y\left(1\right) = - 1$
Then the value of ${\left(y\left(3\right)\right)}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
We have,

${e}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}dx + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = 0, y\left(1\right) = - 1$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}dx = \left(\dfrac{- y}{x}\right)dy$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{- y}{\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}}dy = ∫ x{e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{d\left(1 - {y}^{2}\right)}{\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}}dy = ∫ x{e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}} = {e}^{x}\left(x - 1\right) + c$

Now, at $x = 1, y = - 1$, then

$⇒ 0 = 0 + c ⇒ c = 0$

$∴ \sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}} = {e}^{x}\left(x - 1\right)$

At $x = 3$, then

$\sqrt{1 - {\left(y\left(3\right)\right)}^{2}} = 2{e}^{3}$

$⇒ 1 - {\left(y\left(3\right)\right)}^{2} = 4{e}^{6}$

$⇒ {\left(y\left(3\right)\right)}^{2} = 1 - 4{e}^{6}$

questions.solution:
Let $y + 1 = Y$

$∴ \dfrac{dY}{dx} = {Y}^{2}e\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - xY$

Put $- \dfrac{1}{Y} = k$

$⇒ \dfrac{dk}{dx} + k\left(- x\right) = e\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

$I . F . = {e}^{- \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}}$

$∴ k = \left(x + c\right){e}^{{x}^{2} / 2}$

Put $k = - \dfrac{1}{y + 1}$

$∴ y + 1 = - \dfrac{1}{( x + c ) {e}^{{x}^{2} / 2}} . . . \left(i\right)$

when $x = 2, y = 0$, then $c = - 2 - \dfrac{1}{{e}^{2}}$

Differentiate equation $( i ) \text{ and }$ put $x = 1$ we get,

${\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}_{x = 1} = - \dfrac{{e}^{3 / 2}}{{\left(1 + {e}^{2}\right)}^{2}}$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $xdy - ydx = \sqrt{\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)}dx, x \ge 1$, with $y ( 1 ) = 0$. If the area bounded by the line $x = 1, x = {e}^{\pi}, y = 0$ and $y = y ( x )$ is $\alpha{e}^{2\pi} + \beta,$ then the value of $10 ( \alpha + \beta )$ is equal to ___ .
questions.solution:
Given $xdy - ydx = \sqrt{{x}^{2} - {y}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}{\sqrt{1 - {\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = ln\left|x\right| + c$

at $x = 1, y = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

$y = xsin ( lnx )$

$A = {∫}_{1}^{{e}^{\pi}}xsin\left(lnx\right)dx$

$x = {e}^{t}, dx = {e}^{t}dt ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{2t}sin\left(t\right)dt = A$

$\alpha{e}^{2\pi} + \beta = {\left(\dfrac{{e}^{2t}}{5} ( 2sint - cost )\right)}_{0}^{\pi} = \dfrac{1 + {e}^{2\pi}}{5}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{5}, \beta = \dfrac{1}{5}$

So, $10 ( \alpha + \beta ) = 4$

questions.solution:
${y}^{2} = 4ax + 4{a}^{2}$

differentiate with respect to $x$

$⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a$

$⇒ a = \left(\dfrac{y}{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)$

$⇒ {y}^{2}{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2} + 2xy\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) - {y}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ y{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2} + 2x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) - y = 0$
