questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) dy = ( 1 + ysinx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) ) dx, 0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}, y\left(0\right) = 0 .$ Then, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) dy = ( 1 + ysinx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) ) dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{( 1 + ysinx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) )}{cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 )}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 )} + \dfrac{ysinx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) )}{cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 )}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - ( tanx ) y = \dfrac{1}{( 3sinx + cosx + 3 ) cosx}$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = - tanx$ and $Q = \dfrac{1}{cosx\left(3sinx + cosx + 3\right)} .$

Now, the integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ - tanxdx}$

$= {e}^{ln\left|cosx\right|} = \left|cosx\right|$

$= cosx ∀ 0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

The solution of the given differential equation is $y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ ( cosx ) \cdot \dfrac{1}{cosx ( 3sinx + cosx + 3 )}dx + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{3sinx + cosx + 3}dx + C$

Using $sin2\theta = \dfrac{2tan\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta} \text{ and } cos2\theta = \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{3 \times \dfrac{2tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{1 + \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}} + \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}{1 + \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}} + 3}dx + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}{6tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 3 + 3\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}dx + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left({sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 6tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 4}dx + C$

Let ${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{\left({sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2\left(\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 3tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 2\right)}dx + C$

Put $tan\dfrac{x}{2} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{3} + 3t + 2} = ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left(t + 2\right) ( t + 1 )}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{t + 1} - \dfrac{1}{t + 2}\right)dt$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(t + 1\right) - {\log}_{e}\left(t + 2\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{t + 1}{t + 2}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left|\left(\dfrac{tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 1}{tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 2}\right)\right|$

So, the solution is $y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left|\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right| + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right) + C$ for $0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

Now, it is given $y ( 0 ) = 0$

$⇒ 0 = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + C ⇒ C = {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

Now, for $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3},$y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{3} + 1}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{3} + 1}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{3} - 1}\right)\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{5 + \sqrt{3}}{11}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y = 2{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3} + 10}{11}\right) .$

Using $sin2\theta = \dfrac{2tan\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta} \text{ and } cos2\theta = \dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}{6tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 3 + 3\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}dx + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left({sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 6tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 4}dx + C$

Let ${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{\left({sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2\left(\tan^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} + 3tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 2\right)}dx + C$

Put $tan\dfrac{x}{2} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{3} + 3t + 2} = ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left(t + 2\right) ( t + 1 )}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{t + 1} - \dfrac{1}{t + 2}\right)dt$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(t + 1\right) - {\log}_{e}\left(t + 2\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{t + 1}{t + 2}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left|\left(\dfrac{tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 1}{tan\dfrac{x}{2} + 2}\right)\right|$

So, the solution is $y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left|\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right| + C$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right) + C$ for $0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

Now, it is given $y ( 0 ) = 0$

$⇒ 0 = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + C ⇒ C = {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y\left(cosx\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}{2 + tan\dfrac{x}{2}}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

Now, for $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3},$y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{3} + 1}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{3} + 1}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{3} - 1}\right)\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{5 + \sqrt{3}}{11}\right) + {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ y = 2{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3} + 10}{11}\right) .$

questions.q: If the curve $y = y ( x )$ is the solution of the differential equation $2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2{x}^{9 / 4}dx, x > 0$ which passes through the point $\left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right),$ then the value of $y ( 16 )$ is equal to <gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is $2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2{x}^{9 / 4}dx$

$⇒ 2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right) = 2{x}^{9 / 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2x\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2{x}^{5 / 4}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{2x} = \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = - \dfrac{1}{2x}$ and $Q = \dfrac{x}{{x}^{3 / 4} + 1}$

Now, we have integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$= {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}x}$

$= {e}^{{\log}_{e}{x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}} = {x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, the solution of the linear differential equation is $y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q \times \left(I . F .\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{x \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

Put $x = {t}^{4} ⇒ dx = 4{t}^{3}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2} \cdot 4{t}^{3}dt}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}\left({t}^{3} + 1 - 1\right)}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3} + 1}dt + C$

Let, ${t}^{3} + 1 = u ⇒ 3{t}^{2}dt = du$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - \dfrac{4}{3} ∫ \dfrac{du}{u} + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left|u\right| + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({t}^{3} + 1\right) + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{x}^{3 / 4}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) + C$

Now, the curve passes through $\left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right)$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 + C$

$⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{3 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{5 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{x}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{3}$

Hence, at $x = 16,$ we get

$y ( 16 ) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 32 - \dfrac{4}{3} \times 4 \times {\log}_{e}9 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = \dfrac{124}{3} - \dfrac{32}{3}{\log}_{e}3$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = 4\left(\dfrac{31}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}{\log}_{e}3\right) .

$

questions.explanation:
Given differential equation is $2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2{x}^{9 / 4}dx$

$⇒ 2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right) = 2{x}^{9 / 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2\left({x}^{2} + {x}^{5 / 4}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)}{2x\left(x + {x}^{1 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2{x}^{9 / 4}}{2{x}^{5 / 4}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{2x} = \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = - \dfrac{1}{2x}$ and $Q = \dfrac{x}{{x}^{3 / 4} + 1}$

Now, we have integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$= {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}x}$

$= {e}^{{\log}_{e}{x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}} = {x}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, the solution of the linear differential equation is $y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q \times \left(I . F .\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{x \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{1 / 2}}{\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}dx + C$

Put $x = {t}^{4} ⇒ dx = 4{t}^{3}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2} \cdot 4{t}^{3}dt}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}\left({t}^{3} + 1 - 1\right)}{\left({t}^{3} + 1\right)}dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - 4 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3} + 1}dt + C$

Let, ${t}^{3} + 1 = u ⇒ 3{t}^{2}dt = du$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ {t}^{2}dt - \dfrac{4}{3} ∫ \dfrac{du}{u} + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left|u\right| + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{t}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({t}^{3} + 1\right) + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4{x}^{3 / 4}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) + C$

Now, the curve passes through $\left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2\right)$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}2 + C$

$⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y \cdot {x}^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{3 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4}{3}{x}^{5 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{x}{\log}_{e}\left({x}^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{3}$

Hence, at $x = 16,$ we get

$y ( 16 ) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 32 - \dfrac{4}{3} \times 4 \times {\log}_{e}9 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = \dfrac{124}{3} - \dfrac{32}{3}{\log}_{e}3$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = 4\left(\dfrac{31}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}{\log}_{e}3\right) .

$

questions.q:
Which of the following is true for $y\left(x\right)$ that satisfies the differential equation

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = xy - 1 + x - y; y\left(0\right) = 0$
questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(1 + y\right)\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{( y + 1 )} = \left(x - 1\right)dx$

Integrate both the sides we get,

$ln\left(y + 1\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - x + c$

Given $y\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

$∴ y = {e}^{\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - x\right)} - 1$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(tanx\right)y = sinx; 0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ tanxdx} = {e}^{lnsecx} = secx$

$ysecx = ∫ tanxdx + C$

$ysecx = ln\left|secx\right| + C$

$x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ C = 0$

$ysecx = ln\left|secx\right|$

$y = cosx \cdot ln\left|secx\right|$

${y}_{x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cdot ln\sqrt{2}$

${y}_{x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}{\log}_{e}2$

questions.q: Let ${C}_{1}$ be the curve obtained by the solution of differential equation $2xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = {y}^{2} - {x}^{2}, x > 0$. Let the curve ${C}_{2}$ be the solution of $\dfrac{2xy}{{x}^{2} - {y}^{2}} = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$. If both the curves pass through $\left(1, 1\right),$ then the area (in sq. units) enclosed by the curves ${C}_{1} and {C}_{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{y}^{2} - {x}^{2}}{2xy}, x \in \left(0, \infty\right)$

put $y = vx$

$x\dfrac{dv}{dx} + v = \dfrac{{v}^{2} - 1}{2v}$

$\dfrac{2v}{{v}^{2} + 1}dv = - \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Integrate,
$ln\left({v}^{2} + 1\right) = - lnx + C$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + 1\right) = - lnx + C$

put $x = 1, y = 1, C = ln2$

$ln\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + 1\right) = - lnx + ln2$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x = 0$ (Curve ${C}_{1}$)

Similarly,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy}{{x}^{2} - {y}^{2}}$

Put $y = vx$

${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2y = 0$

Required area $= 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt{2x - {x}^{2}} - x\right)dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1$ sq. units

questions.q: If $y = y\left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ytanx = sinx, y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 0$, then the maximum value of the function $y\left(x\right)$ over $R$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ytanx = sinx$

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ 2tanxdx} = {e}^{2lnsecx}$

$I . F . = {sec}^{2}x$

$y . \left({sec}^{2}x\right) = ∫ sinx . {sec}^{2}xdx + C$

$y . \left({sec}^{2}x\right) = ∫ secxtanxdx + C$

$y . \left({sec}^{2}x\right) = secx + C$

$x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}; y = 0$

$⇒ C = - 2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{secx - 2}{{sec}^{2}x} = cosx - 2\cos^{2}x$

Let $cosx = t, - 1 \le t \le 1$

$⇒ y = t - 2{t}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 1 - 4t = 0 ⇒ t = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Second-order derivative is negative

$∴ max = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

questions.q: Let slope of the tangent line to a curve at any point $P\left(x, y\right)$ be given by $\dfrac{x{y}^{2} + y}{x}$. If the curve intersects the line $x + 2y = 4$ at $x = - 2$, then the value of $y$, for which the point $\left(3, y\right)$ lies on the curve, is :
questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x{y}^{2} + y}{x}$

$\dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{y}^{2}} = xdx$

$- d\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = xdx$

$- \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + c$

$∵$ Curve intersects the line $x + 2y = 4$ at $x = - 2 ⇒$ point of intersection is $\left(- 2, 3\right)$.

$∴$ Curve passes through $\left(- 2, 3\right)$.

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3} = 2 + c ⇒ c = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- x}{y} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now put $\left(3, y\right)$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{- 3}{y} = \dfrac{19}{6}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{- 18}{19}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The rate of growth of bacteria in a culture is proportional to the number of bacteria present and the bacteria count is $1000$ at initial time $t = 0 .$ The number of bacteria is increased by $20 %$ in $2$ hours. If the population of bacteria is $2000$ after $\dfrac{k}{{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)}$ hours, then ${\left(\dfrac{k}{{\log}_{e}2}\right)}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{dB}{dt} ∝ B ⇒ \dfrac{dB}{dt} = \lambdaB, \left(\lambda\text{is proportionility constant}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dB}{B} = \lambdadt$

Integrate both sides with proper limit we get,

${∫}_{{B}_{1}}^{{B}_{2}}\dfrac{dB}{B} = {∫}_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\lambdadt$

$⇒ ln\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \lambda\left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Given that, at $t = 0, B = 1000 \text{ and } t = 20 % \text{increase} = 1200$

$∴ ln\dfrac{1200}{1000} = 2\lambda ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}$

Now an equation $\left(i\right)$becomes,

$ln\dfrac{{B}_{2}}{{B}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}\left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Given that, at ${t}_{2} = \dfrac{k}{ln2}, {B}_{2} = 2000 \text{ and } t = 0, {B}_{1} = 1000$

From $\left(ii\right), ln\dfrac{2000}{1000} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\dfrac{6}{5}\left(\dfrac{k}{ln\dfrac{6}{5}} - 0\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}k$

$⇒ k = 2ln2$

$∴ {\left(\dfrac{k}{ln2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{2ln2}{ln2}\right)}^{2} = 4$

questions.q: The difference between degree and order of a differential equation that represents the family of curves given by ${y}^{2} = a\left(x + \dfrac{\sqrt{a}}{2}\right), a > 0$ is _______.
questions.solution:
${y}^{2} = a\left(x + \dfrac{\sqrt{a}}{2}\right) = ax + \dfrac{{a}^{3 / 2}}{2}$. . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 2y{y}^{'} = a$

Put in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

${y}^{2} = \left(2y{y}^{'}\right)x + \dfrac{{\left(2y{y}^{'}\right)}^{3 / 2}}{2}$

$\left({y}^{2} - 2xy{y}^{'}\right) = \dfrac{{\left(2y{y}^{'}\right)}^{3 / 2}}{2}$

Squaring both the sides we get,

${\left({y}^{2} - 2xy{y}^{'}\right)}^{2} = 2{y}^{3}{\left({y}^{'}\right)}^{3}$

$∴$ Order $= 1$

Degree $= 3$

Degree $-$ order $= 3 - 1 = 2$

questions.solution:
Put ${e}^{siny} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{siny}cosy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ D . E$ is $\dfrac{dt}{dx} + tcosx = cosx$

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ cosxdx} = {e}^{sinx}$

$⇒$ solution is $t . {e}^{sinx} = ∫ cosx{e}^{sinx}$

$⇒ {e}^{siny}{e}^{sinx} = {e}^{sinx} + c$

$∵ x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

$⇒ {e}^{siny} = 1$

$⇒ y = 0$

$⇒ 1 + y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$

questions.q: If the curve, $y = y \left(x\right) represented by$ the $solution of the differential equation \left(2x{y}^{2} - y\right)dx + xdy = 0$, passes through the intersection of the lines, $2x - 3y = 1 and 3x + 2y = 8$, then $| y\left(1\right) |$ is equal to ___ .
questions.solution:
$\left(2x{y}^{2} - y\right)dx + xdy = 0$

$2x{y}^{2}dx - ydx + xdy = 0$

$2xdx = \dfrac{ydx - xdy}{{y}^{2}} = d\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)$

Now integrate

${x}^{2} = \dfrac{x}{y} + c$

Now point of intersection of lines are $\left(2, 1\right)$.

$4 = \dfrac{2}{1} + c ⇒ c = 2$

${x}^{2} = \dfrac{x}{y} + 2$

Now $y\left(1\right) = - 1$

$⇒ | y\left(1\right) | = 1$

questions.q: If a curve passes through the origin and the slope of the tangent to it at any point $\left(x, y\right)$ is $\dfrac{{x}^{2} - 4x + y + 8}{x - 2},$ then this curve also passes through the point:
questions.solution:
Given

$y\left(0\right) = 0$

and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{2} + y + 4}{x - 2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x - 2} = \left(x - 2\right) + \dfrac{4}{x - 2}$

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{1}{x - 2}dx} = \dfrac{1}{x - 2}$

$⇒ y\dfrac{1}{x - 2} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x - 2}\left(\left(x - 2\right) + \dfrac{4}{x - 2}\right) \cdot dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x - 2} = x - \dfrac{4}{x - 2} + C$

Now, at $x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ C = - 2$

$y = x\left(x - 2\right) - 4 - 2\left(x - 2\right)$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2} - 4x$

This curve passes through $\left(5, 5\right)$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable function defined on $R$ such that $f\left(0\right) = 1, {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = 2$ and ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) \ne 0$ for all $x \in R .$ If $\left|\begin{cases}f\left(x\right) & {f}^{'}\left(x\right) \\ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) & {f}^{''}\left(x\right)\end{cases}\right| = 0,$ for all $x \in R,$ then the value of $f\left(1\right)$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
We have, $\left|\begin{cases}f\left(x\right) & {f}^{'}\left(x\right) \\ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) & {f}^{' '}\left(x\right)\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ f\left(x\right){f}^{' '}\left(x\right) - {\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}^{' '}\left(x\right)}{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)}$

On integrating both side, we get

$ln\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right) = lnf\left(x\right) + lnc$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = cf \left(x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} = c$

Again integrating, we get

$lnf\left(x\right) = cx + {k}_{1}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = k{e}^{cx}$

Since, $f\left(0\right) = 1 = k$

Therefore, ${f}^{'}\left(0\right) = c = 2$

Now, $f\left(x\right) = {e}^{2x}$

Hence, $f\left(1\right) = {e}^{2} \in \left(6, 9\right)$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {f}^{'}\left(2 - x\right)$

put $x = 0$

$c = f\left(0\right) + f\left(2\right) = 1 + {e}^{2}$

so, $f\left(x\right) + f\left(2 - x\right) = 1 + {e}^{2}$

$2I = \left(1 + {e}^{2}\right){∫}_{0}^{2}dx$

$I = 1 + {e}^{2}$

$⇒ In\left|P\left(t\right) - 900\right| - In\left|P\left(0\right) - 900\right| = \dfrac{t}{2}$

$⇒ In\left|P\left(t\right) - 900\right| - In\left|50\right| = \dfrac{t}{2}$

for $P\left(t\right) = 0$

$⇒ In\left|\dfrac{900}{50}\right| = \dfrac{t}{2} ⇒ t = 2In18$

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + {x}^{2}{y}^{2}} + xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$ (where C is a constant of integration)
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {y}^{2}\right)} + xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Integrating,

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{2y}{2\sqrt{1 + {y}^{2}}}\right)dy = - ∫ \left(\dfrac{1 + {x}^{2}}{x\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + {y}^{2}} = - ∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}}dx - ∫ \dfrac{x}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}}dx$

Put $\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} = t ⇒ {x}^{2} = {t}^{2} - 1$ to solve RHS 2nd integration,

$⇒ \sqrt{1 + {y}^{2}} = - \sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} - ∫ \dfrac{t}{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)t}dt$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + {y}^{2}} + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} = - ∫ \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2} - 1}dt$
$⇒ \sqrt{1 + {y}^{2}} + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} + 1}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} - 1}\right] + C$

Given $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = {x}^{2}\left(xcos + sinx\right)$

$⇒$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{x}y = x\left(xcosx + sinx\right)$

$= - {x}^{2}sinx + 4xcosx + 2sinx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2$.

questions.solution:

questions.solution:

Separate variables

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + {y}^{2}\right)dy}{{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{dx}{1 + {e}^{- x}}$

Integrate both side

$⇒ ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}\right)dy = ∫ \dfrac{{e}^{x}dx}{{e}^{x} + 1}$

$⇒ y - \dfrac{1}{y} = ln\left({e}^{x} + 1\right) + C$

Since curve pass through $\left(0, 1\right)$.

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{1}{1} = ln\left({e}^{0} + 1\right) + C ⇒ C = - ln\left(2\right)

$⇒ y - $\dfrac{1}{y} =$ln $\left({e}^{x} + 1\right)$ - ln $\left(2\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{y}^{2} - 1}{y} = ln\left(\dfrac{{e}^{x} + 1}{2}\right)

$⇒ {y}^{2} = 1 + y{$\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 + {e}^{x}}{2}\right)

questions.q: If a curve $y = f \left(x\right), passing through$ the $point \left(1, 2\right), is the solution of the differential equation$2{x}^{2}dy = $\left(2xy + {y}^{2}\right)$dx$, then $f$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}$\right)$ is equal to$
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ {y}^{- 2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{y} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2{x}^{2}}$

Put $- \dfrac{1}{y} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)t = \dfrac{1}{2{x}^{2}}$

This is a linear differential equation,

with Integrating Factor : ${e}^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = {e}^{ln\left(x\right)} = x$

So, solution of the linear differential equation is $tx = ∫ \dfrac{1}{2{x}^{2}} \cdot xdx + C$

$⇒ - \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(x\right) + C$

The curve passes through $\left(1, 2\right)$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(1\right) + C ⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the particular solution to the differential equation is $- \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(x\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1 - ln\left(x\right)}{2} ⇒ y = \dfrac{2x}{1 - ln\left(x\right)}$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{1 + ln\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{1 + {\log}_{e}\left(2\right)}$

$⇒ x = 2 - e$

questions.q: Consider the differential equation, ${y}^{2}dx + \left(x - \dfrac{1}{y}\right)dy = 0$. If value of $y$ is $1$ when $x = 1$, then the value of $x$ for which $y = 2,$is
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
${y}^{2}dx = \left(\dfrac{1}{y} - x\right)dy$

$⇒ {y}^{2}\dfrac{dx}{dy} + x = \dfrac{1}{y}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{1}{{y}^{3}}$
It is a linear differential equation whose integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{dy}{{y}^{2}}} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}$
Solution of a given differential equation can be written as
$x{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{y}} = ∫ {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}\dfrac{1}{{y}^{3}}dy = I$
Let $\dfrac{- 1}{y} = t ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{{y}^{2}} = dt ⇒ I = ∫ \left(- t\right){e}^{t}dt$
$= {e}^{t}\left(1 - t\right) + C$, (Integrating by parts)
$⇒$ Solution of differential equation is $x{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{y}} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{y}}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{y}\right) + C$
Since for $x = 1,$we have $y = 1$,
$⇒ 1 . {e}^{- 1} = {e}^{- 1}\left(1 + 1\right) + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{- 1}{e}$
$⇒$ Solution with given condition is $x{e}^{\dfrac{- 1}{y}} = {e}^{\dfrac{- 1}{y}}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{y}\right) - {e}^{- 1}$
or $x = 1 + \dfrac{1}{y} - {e}^{\left(\dfrac{1}{y} - 1\right)}$
So, ${\leftx\right|}_{y = 2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} - {e}^{\dfrac{1}{2} - 1} = \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}$

questions.solution:
Given $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = 2x + {x}^{2}tanx$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P = tanx \text{ and } Q = 2x + {x}^{2}tanx$

Now, the integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ tanxdx}$

$= {e}^{lnsecx} = secx$

And, the general solution is $y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$y ⋅ secx = ∫ \left(2x + {x}^{2}tanx\right)secxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + ∫ {x}^{2}\left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx + c$

Using integration by parts in the second integral, we get

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + {x}^{2} ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx - ∫ \left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({x}^{2}\right) ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + {x}^{2} ∫ secxdx - ∫ 2xsecxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = {x}^{2}secx + c$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2} + c \cdot cosx$

Now, $y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ 0 + c = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

So, $y = {x}^{2} + cosx$

Hence, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Differentiating $y ( x )$ with respect to $x$

$⇒ {y}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x - sinx$

Hence, ${y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and ${y}^{'}\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ {y}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - {y}^{'}\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \pi - \sqrt{2} .$

questions.solution:
Given, differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)y = x$

This is a linear differential equation of type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P \text{ and } Q$ are the functions of $x$ or constants.

Thus, $P = \dfrac{2}{x} \text{ and } Q = x$

The integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = {e}^{2lnx}$

$= {e}^{ln{x}^{2}} = {x}^{2} .$

The solution of the linear differential equation is $y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(Q \times I . F .\right)dx + C$

So, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y{x}^{2} = ∫ x \cdot {x}^{2}dx + C$

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = ∫ {x}^{3}dx + C$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1},$ we get

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} + C$

Since $y\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 \cdot 1 = \dfrac{1}{4} + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4{x}^{2}} .$

questions.solution:

Hence, the solution of the given differential equation is

$⇒ y \cdot x = {\log}_{e}x\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) - ∫ \dfrac{x}{2}dx$

$⇒ xy\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}{\log}_{e}x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + C . . . \left(1\right)$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation, $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=(x-y)^{2}$, when $y(1)=1,$ is:
questions.solution:
The given differential equation

$\frac{d y}{d x}=(x-y)^{2}$

Let $x-y=t \Rightarrow 1-\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x} \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=1-\frac{d t}{d x}$

Now, from equation (1)

$\left(1-\frac{d t}{d x}\right)=(t)^{2} \Rightarrow \quad 1-t^{2}=\frac{d t}{d x} \Rightarrow \int d x=\int \frac{d t}{1-t^{2}} \Rightarrow-x=\frac{1}{2 \times 1} \ln \left|\frac{t-1}{t+1}\right|+c \Rightarrow-x=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{x-y-1}{x-y+1}\right|+c \because$ The given condition $y(1)=1 -1=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{1-1-1}{1-1+1}\right|+c \Rightarrow c=-1$

Hence, $2(x-1)=-\ln \left|\frac{1-x+y}{1-y+x}\right|$

questions.q: If $y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{2 x+1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x>0,$ where $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2},$ then:
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is,

$\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x>0$\mathrm{IF}=e^{\int\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) d x}=e^{2 x+\ln x}=x e^{2 x}$

Complete solution is given by

$y(x) \cdot x e^{2 x}=\int x e^{2 x} \cdot e^{-2 x} d x+c$=\int x d x+c$y(x) \cdot e^{2 x} \cdot x=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+c$

Given, $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2}$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{2} e^{-2} \cdot e^{2} \cdot 1=\frac{1}{2}+c \Rightarrow c=0$\therefore \quad y(x)=\frac{x^{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{e^{-2 x}}{x}$y(x)=\frac{x}{2} \cdot e^{-2 x}$

Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$y^{\prime}(x)=\frac{e^{-2 x}}{2}(1-2 x)  < 0 \forall x \in\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$

Hence, $y(x)$ is decreasing in $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a polynomial function such that $f\left(3x\right) = {f}^{′}\left(x\right) . {f}^{′′}\left(x\right),$ for all $x \in R .$ Then :
questions.solution:
Degree of $f\left(x\right)$ will be $3$

$f ( x) = a{x}^{3} + b{x}^{2} + cx + d$

$f\left(3x\right) = 27a{x}^{3} + 9b{x}^{2} + 3cx + d$

${f}^{'} ( x ) = 3a{x}^{2} + 2bx + c$

${f}^{′′}\left(x\right) = 6ax + 2b$

$f\left(3x\right) = {f}^{′}\left(x\right){f}^{′′}\left(x\right)$

Comparing the coefficient, we get

$27a = 18{a}^{2}$⇒ a = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Also $b = 0, c = 0, d = 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{3}$, $f( 2 ) = 12$

$⇒ {f}^{′}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{9}{2}{x}^{2}, {f}^{′′}\left(x\right) = 9x$

Hence, ${f}^{'}( 2 ) = 18, f{}^{''} ( 2 ) = 18$

Hence, ${f}^{''}\left(2\right) - f ' ( 2 ) = 0$

questions.q: A tangent to the curve, $y = f\left(x\right)$ at $P\left(x, y\right)$ meets $x$-axis at <mrow>$A$ </mrow> and $y$-axis at <mrow>$B$. If $AP: BP = 1: 3$ and $f\left(1\right) = 1,$ then the curve also passes through the point</mrow>
questions.solution:
Equation of tangent,

$\begin{array}{ll}Y - y = \dfrac{dy}{dx} ( X - x ) \\ A( x - y\dfrac{dx}{dy} , 0 )\text{​}: B( 0, y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} )\end{array}$

Given, $AP: BP = 1: 3$,

Using section formula, we get

$y = \dfrac{y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{4}$

$⇒ y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} + 3\dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$

By integrating w.r.t $x$, we get

$ln | y | + 3ln | x | = lnc$

$| y{x}^{3} | = c$

$∵ f ( 1 ) = 1$

$∴ c = 1$

$⇒ | y{x}^{3} | = 1$

Hence, the curve passes throught the point $\left(2, \dfrac{1}{8}\right)$

questions.q: The curve satisfying the differential equation, $ydx - \left(x + 3{y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ and passing through the point $( 1, 1 )$ also passes through the point
questions.solution:
Given differential equation, $ydx - xdy - 3{y}^{2}dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x}{y} + 3y$

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{x}{y} = 3y$

I.F. = ${e}^{- ∫ \dfrac{1}{y}dy} = {e}^{- ln ⁡ y} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

$∴$ solution is

$\dfrac{x}{y} = ∫ 3y . \dfrac{1}{y}dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = 3y + c$

Passes through $( 1, 1 )$,

$∴ 1 = 3 + c; c = - 2$

Equation of required curve, $x = 3{y}^{2} - 2y$

Clearly, it passes through $\left(\dfrac{- 1}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$.

questions.q: If $\left(2 + sinx\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(y + 1\right)cosx = 0$ and $y\left(0\right) = 1$, then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,

$\left(2 + sinx\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(y + 1\right)cosx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{\left(y + 1\right)} = - ∫ \dfrac{cosx}{sinx + 2}dx$

Let, $sinx = t⇒ cosxdx = dt$

$⇒ log\left|y + 1\right| = - ∫ \dfrac{dt}{t + 2} + C$

where, $C$ is the constant of integration.

$⇒ log\left|y + 1\right| + log\left|sinx + 2\right| - C = 0$

$⇒ log\left(y + 1\right)\left(sinx + 2\right) = C$

Given, $y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ C = log4$.

$⇒ log\left(y + 1\right)\left(sinx + 2\right) = log4 . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ in the equation $\left(i\right)$, we get, $log\left(y + 1\right) + log\left(3\right) - log\left(4\right) = 0$

$⇒ log\left(y + 1\right) = log\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$

$⇒ y + 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4}{3} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{2}sec ⁡ x = \dfrac{tan ⁡ x}{2y}$
$2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {y}^{2}sec ⁡ x = tan ⁡ x$
Put ${y}^{2} = t ⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$
$\dfrac{dt}{dx} + tsec ⁡ x = tan ⁡ x$
$I . F = {e}^{∫ sec ⁡ xdx} = {e}^{ln ( sec ⁡ x + tanx )} = sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x$
$⇒ t\left(sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x\right) = ∫ \left(sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x\right)tan ⁡ xdx$
$⇒ t\left(sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x\right) = ∫ \left(sec ⁡ xtan ⁡ x\right)dx + ∫ \tan^{2} ⁡ xdx$
$⇒ {y}^{2}\left(sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x\right) = sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x - x + c$
$y\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 0$
$⇒ {y}^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{x}{sec ⁡ x + tan ⁡ x}$

The given differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = sin2x$ is linear differential equation of the form

Now, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ P \left(x\right)dx} = {e}^{∫ tanx dx} = {e}^{ln\left(sec x\right)} = secx$

And, the solution is $y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(x\right)\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ secxsin2xdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ \dfrac{1}{cosx}\left(2sinxcosx\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2sinxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = - 2cosx + c$

Given, $y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 \cdot sec0 = - 2cos0 + c$

$⇒ 1 = - 2 + c$

$⇒ c = 3$

$⇒ ysec x = - 2cosx + 3$

Now, at $x = \pi$

$y\left(\pi\right)sec\pi = - 2cos\pi + 3$

$⇒ y\left(\pi\right)\left(- 1\right) = - 2\left(- 1\right) + 3$

$⇒ y\left(\pi\right) = - 5 .$

questions.q: If for a continuous function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$, $\int_{-\pi}^t(f(x)+x d x)=\pi^2-t^2$, for all $t \geq-\pi$, then $\mathrm{f}\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is equal to:

Let $\int_{-\pi}^t(f(x)+x) d x=\pi^2-t^2 \begin{aligned}$&\Rightarrow \int_{-$\pi$}^t f(x) d x+\int_{-$\pi$}^t x d x=$\pi^$2-t² \\
&\Rightarrow \int_{-$\pi$}^t f(x) d x+$\left(\frac{t^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{2}\right)=\pi^$2-t² \\
&\Rightarrow \int_{-$\pi$}^t f(x) d x=$\frac{3}{2}\left(\pi^$2-t²\right)
\end{aligned}

questions.q: If the general solution of the differential equation $y^{\prime}=\frac{y}{x}+\Phi\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)$, for some function $\Phi$, is given by $y \ln |c x|=x$, where $\mathrm{c}$ is an arbitrary constant, then $\Phi(2)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{x}+\phi \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)
Let \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=$v$ so that $y=x v or $\frac{d y}{d x}=$x $\frac{d v}{d x}+$v$
from (1) \& (2), $x $\frac{d v}{d x}+$v=v+\phi $\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)$ or, $\frac{d v}{\phi\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)}=\frac{d x}{x}$
Integrating both sides, we get $\int \frac{d x}{x}=\int \frac{d v}{\phi\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)} \Rightarrow \ln x+c=\int \frac{d v}{\phi\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)}$
(where $\mathrm{c}$ being constant of integration)
But, given $\mathrm{y}=\frac{x}{\ln |c x|}$ is the general solution
so that $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{1}{v}=\ln |c x|=\int \frac{d v}{\phi\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)}$
Differentiating w.r.t $v$ both sides, we get $\phi\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)=\frac{-1}{v^2} \Rightarrow \phi\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)=-\frac{y^2}{x^2}$
when $\frac{x}{y}=2$ i.e. $\phi(2)$
=-$\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^$2=-$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^$2=$\left(\frac{-1}{4}\right)$

questions.q: If the differential equation representing the family of all circles touching $x$-axis at the origin is $\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g\left(x\right)y$, then $g\left(x\right)$ equals
questions.solution:
Equation of circle touching $x$-axis in origin is ${\left(x - 0\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - k\right)}^{2} = {k}^{2}$
$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2ky = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$, where $k$ is the radius of the circle.

Differentiating the above equation w.r.t. $x$, we get,

$2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2k\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ x + \left(y - k\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

From equation $\left(1\right)$,

$⇒ x + \left(y - \dfrac{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}{2y}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2xy = g\left(x\right)y$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 2x$

questions.q: The equation of the curve passing through the origin and satisfying the differential equation $\left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x y=4 x^2$ is
options:
$\left(1+x^2\right) y=x^3$

$3\left(1+x^2\right) y=2 x^3$

$\left(1+x^2\right) y=3 x^3$

$3\left(1+x^2\right) y=4 x^3$
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is
$
\begin{aligned}
&\left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x y=4 x^2 \\
&\Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}\right) y=\frac{4 x^2}{1+x^2}
\end{aligned}
$
This is linear diff. equation
$
\mathrm{I} . \mathrm{F}=e^{\int \frac{2 x}{1+x^2} d x}=e^{\log \left(1+x^2\right)}=1+x^2
$
Solution is
$
\begin{aligned}
&y\left(1+x^2\right)=\int \frac{4 x^2}{1+x^2} \times 1+x^2+\mathrm{C} \\
&\Rightarrow y\left(1+x^2\right)=\frac{4 x^3}{3}+\mathrm{C} \\
&\Rightarrow \text{ Required curve is } \\
&3 y\left(1+x^2\right)=4 x^3(\because \mathrm{C}=0)
\end{aligned}
$

questions.q: Solution of the differential equation $\cos x d y=y(\sin x-y) d x, 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$ is
options:
$y \sec x=\tan x+c$

$y \tan x=\sec x+c$

$\tan x=(\sec x+c) y$

 $\sec x=(\tan x+c) y$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}$& \cos x d y=y(\sin x-y) d x \\
& $\frac{d y}{d x}=$y \tan x-y² \sec x \\
& $\frac{1}{y^2} \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{1}{y} \tan$x=-\sec x \\
& $\text{ Let } \frac{1}{y}=$t \\
& -$\frac{1}{y^2} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x}$\\
& -$\frac{d y}{d x}-$t \tan x=-\sec x \Rightarrow $\frac{d t}{d x}+(\tan$x) t=\sec x . \\
& $\text{ I.F. }=$e^{f \tan x d x}=\sec x
\end{aligned}

Solution is $t\left(\right.$ I.F) $=\int$ (I.F) $\sec x d x\frac{1}{y} \sec x=\tan x+c$

& \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x}=\log$ x+c

questions.q: The differential equation of all circles passing through the origin and having their centres on the $x$-axis is
options:
$x^2=y^2+x y \frac{d y}{d x}$

$x^2=y^2+3 x y \frac{d y}{d x}$

$y^2=x^2+2 x y \frac{d y}{d x}$

$y^2=x^2-2 x y \frac{d y}{d x}$
questions.solution:
General equation of all such circles is 
$\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{gx}=0$.
Differentiating, we get
$2 \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+2 \mathrm{g}=0 \therefore$ Desired equation is
$\begin{aligned}
& x^2+y^2+\left(-2 x-2 y \frac{d y}{d x}\right) x=0 \\
& \Rightarrow y^2=x^2+2 x y \frac{d y}{d x}.
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x d y}{d x}=y(\log y-\log x+1) \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{x}\left(\log \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+1\right)

put $\log v=z$\frac{1}{v} d v=d z$\Rightarrow \frac{d z}{z}=\frac{d x}{x}$\ln z=\ln x+\ln c$z=c x$\log v=c x$\log \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=c x$

questions.q: $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are two differentiable functions on $[0,2]$ such that $f^{\prime \prime}(x)-g^{\prime \prime}(x)=0$f^{\prime}(1)=2 g^{\prime}(1)=4 f(2)=3 g(2)=9$ then $f(x)-g(x)$ at $x=3 / 2$ is
questions.solution:
$\because f^{\prime \prime}(x)-g^{\prime \prime}(x)=0$
Integrating, $f^{\prime}(x)-g^{\prime}(x)=c \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(1)-g^{\prime}(1)=c \Rightarrow 4-2=c \Rightarrow c=2$\therefore f^{\prime}(x)-g^{\prime}(x)=2 ;$ Integrating, $f(x)-g(x)=2 x+c_1$\Rightarrow f(2)-g(2)=4+c_1 \Rightarrow 9-3=4+c_1 \Rightarrow c_1=2 \quad \therefore f(x)-g(x)=2 x+2$
At $x=3 / 2, f(x)-g(x)=3+2=5$
